Śākadvīpa is surrounded on all sides by the ocean of milk,
which is equal [to it] in breadth all around.

1.49.s:
tasmin janapadāḥ puṇyāḥ parvatāntarite śubhāḥ .
varṇāśramasamākīrṇā deśāste sapta vai smṛtāḥ .. 49.99 ..
1.49.d:
तस्मिन् जनपदाः पुण्याः पर्वतान्तरिते शुभाः ।
वर्णाश्रमसमाकीर्णा देशास्ते सप्त वै स्मृताः ॥ 49.99 ॥
1.49.m:
In it are holy, auspicious realms separated by mountains;
those seven regions are recorded as filled with the classes and stages of life.

1.49.s:
na saṅkaraśca teṣvasti varṇāśramakṛtaḥ vkacit .
dharmasya cāvyabhīcārādekāntasukhitāḥ prajāḥ .. 49.100 ..
1.49.d:
न सङ्करश्च तेष्वस्ति वर्णाश्रमकृतः व्कचित् ।
धर्मस्य चाव्यभीचारादेकान्तसुखिताः प्रजाः ॥ 49.100 ॥
1.49.m:
There is no confusion among the classes and stages of life anywhere in them;
and because of the unswerving observance of dharma, the subjects are entirely happy.

1.49.s:
na teṣu lobho māyā vā īrṣyāsūyā'dhṛtiḥ kutaḥ.
viparyayo na teṣvasti etat svābhāvikaṃ smṛtam .. 49.101 ..
1.49.d:
न तेषु लोभो माया वा ईर्ष्यासूयाऽधृतिः कुतः।
विपर्ययो न तेष्वस्ति एतत् स्वाभाविकं स्मृतम् ॥ 49.101 ॥
1.49.m:
Among them there is no greed or deceit; whence could jealousy, spite, or impatience arise?
There is no perversion among them; this is remembered as their inherent nature.

1.49.s:
karotpattirnateṣvasti na daṇḍo na ca daṇḍakāḥ.
svadharmeṇaiva dharmajñāste rakṣanti parasparam .. 49.102 ..
1.49.d:
करोत्पत्तिर्नतेष्वस्ति न दण्डो न च दण्डकाः।
स्वधर्मेणैव धर्मज्ञास्ते रक्षन्ति परस्परम् ॥ 49.102 ॥
1.49.m:
No levying of taxes exists among them, nor punishment, nor punishers.
Knowing dharma, they protect each other solely through their own dharma.

1.49.s:
etāvadeva śakyaṃ vai tasmin dvīpe nivāsinām.
puṣkaraṃ saptamaṃ dvīpaṃ pravakṣyāmi nibodhata .. 49.103 ..
1.49.d:
एतावदेव शक्यं वै तस्मिन् द्वीपे निवासिनाम्।
पुष्करं सप्तमं द्वीपं प्रवक्ष्यामि निबोधत ॥ 49.103 ॥
1.49.m:
Such is all that can be said of those dwelling on that continent.
Now listen: I shall describe the seventh continent, Puṣkara.

1.49.s:
puṣkareṇa tu dvīpena vṛtaḥ kṣīrodako bahiḥ.
śākadvīpasya vistārād‌dviguṇena samantataḥ .. 49.104 ..
1.49.d:
पुष्करेण तु द्वीपेन वृतः क्षीरोदको बहिः।
शाकद्वीपस्य विस्ताराद्‌द्विगुणेन समन्ततः ॥ 49.104 ॥
1.49.m:
The ocean of milk is encircled on the outside by the Puṣkara continent,
which is twice the width of Śākadvīpa all around.

1.49.s:
puṣkare parvataḥ śrīmān eka eva mahāśilaḥ.
citrai rmaṇimayaiḥ śīlaiḥ śikharaistu samucchritaiḥ .. 49.105 ..
1.49.d:
पुष्करे पर्वतः श्रीमान् एक एव महाशिलः।
चित्रै र्मणिमयैः शीलैः शिखरैस्तु समुच्छ्रितैः ॥ 49.105 ॥
1.49.m:
In Puṣkara there is a single, glorious, massive mountain,
with picturesque, gem-studded rocks and lofty peaks.

1.49.s:
dvīpasya tasya pūrvārddhe citrasānuḥ sthito mahān.
parimaṇḍalasahasrāṇi vistīrṇaḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ .. 49.106 ..
1.49.d:
द्वीपस्य तस्य पूर्वार्द्धे चित्रसानुः स्थितो महान्।
परिमण्डलसहस्राणि विस्तीर्णः पञ्चविंशतिः ॥ 49.106 ॥
1.49.m: In the eastern half of that continent stands a great [mountain] with manifold peaks, / twenty-five thousand [yojanas] wide in circumference,

1.49.s:
ūrddvañcaiva catustriśatsahasrāṇi samācitaḥ.
dvīpārddhasya paristomaḥ parvato mānasottamaḥ .. 49.107 ..
1.49.d:
ऊर्द्द्वञ्चैव चतुस्त्रिशत्सहस्राणि समाचितः।
द्वीपार्द्धस्य परिस्तोमः पर्वतो मानसोत्तमः ॥ 49.107 ॥
1.49.m: and stacked thirty-four thousand [yojanas] high; / the most excellent mountain Mānasa surrounds that half of the continent.

1.49.s:
sthito velāsamīpe tu navacandra ivoditaḥ.
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ūrddhvaṃ pañcaśaducchritaḥ .. 49.108 ..
1.49.d:
स्थितो वेलासमीपे तु नवचन्द्र इवोदितः।
योजनानां सहस्राणि ऊर्द्ध्वं पञ्चशदुच्छ्रितः ॥ 49.108 ॥
1.49.m: It stands near the shore like the newly risen moon, / rising upward fifty thousand yojanas.

1.49.s:
tāvadeva sa vistīrṇaḥ sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalaḥ.
sa evaṃ dvīpapaścārddhe mānasaḥ pṛthivīdharaḥ .. 49.109 ..
1.49.d:
तावदेव स विस्तीर्णः सर्वतः परिमण्डलः।
स एवं द्वीपपश्चार्द्धे मानसः पृथिवीधरः ॥ 49.109 ॥
1.49.m: It is just as wide, circular on all sides. / Thus is Mount Mānasa situated in the western half of the continent;

1.49.s:
eka eva mahāsānuḥ sanniveśāddvidhā kṛtaḥ.
svādūdakenodadhinā sarvataḥ parivāritaḥ .. 49.110 ..
1.49.d:
एक एव महासानुः सन्निवेशाद्द्विधा कृतः।
स्वादूदकेनोदधिना सर्वतः परिवारितः ॥ 49.110 ॥
1.49.m: it is a single great-peaked [range], divided in two by its location, / surrounded on all sides by the ocean of fresh water.

1.49.s:
puṣkaradvīpavistārādvistīrṇo'sau samantataḥ.
tasmin dvīpe smṛtau dvau tu puṇyau janapadau śubhau.
abhito mānasasyātha parvatasyānumaṇḍalau .. 49.111 ..
1.49.d:
पुष्करद्वीपविस्ताराद्विस्तीर्णोऽसौ समन्ततः।
तस्मिन् द्वीपे स्मृतौ द्वौ तु पुण्यौ जनपदौ शुभौ।
अभितो मानसस्याथ पर्वतस्यानुमण्डलौ ॥ 49.111 ॥
1.49.m: That [mountain] extends on every side across the breadth of Puṣkaradvīpa. / On that continent are remembered two holy, auspicious regions / forming concentric rings around Mount Mānasa:

1.49.s:
mahāvītantu yadvarṣaṃ bāhyato mānasasya tat.
tasyaivābhyantare yattu dhātakīkhaṇḍamucyate .. 49.112 ..
1.49.d:
महावीतन्तु यद्वर्षं बाह्यतो मानसस्य तत्।
तस्यैवाभ्यन्तरे यत्तु धातकीखण्डमुच्यते ॥ 49.112 ॥
1.49.m: the realm named Mahāvīta is outside Mānasa, / whereas that within it is called Dhātakīkhaṇḍa.

1.49.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tatra jevanti mānavāḥ.
ārogyasukhabhūyiṣṭhā mānasīṃ siddhimāsthitāḥ .. 49.113 ..
1.49.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तत्र जेवन्ति मानवाः।
आरोग्यसुखभूयिष्ठा मानसीं सिद्धिमास्थिताः ॥ 49.113 ॥
1.49.m: Men live there for ten thousand years, / having abundant health and happiness, possessing mental perfection.

1.49.s:
samamāyuśca rūpañca tasmin varṣadvaye sthitam.
adhamottamau na teṣvāstāṃ tulyāste rūpaśīlataḥ .. 49.114 ..
1.49.d:
सममायुश्च रूपञ्च तस्मिन् वर्षद्वये स्थितम्।
अधमोत्तमौ न तेष्वास्तां तुल्यास्ते रूपशीलतः ॥ 49.114 ॥
1.49.m: Equal lifespan and beauty abide in those two realms; / among them there are neither low nor high, for they are equal in beauty and conduct.

1.49.s:
na tatra vañcako nerṣyā na stenā na bhayaṃ tathā.
nigraho na ca daṇḍo'sti na lobho na parigrahaḥ .. 49.115 ..
1.49.d:
न तत्र वञ्चको नेर्ष्या न स्तेना न भयं तथा।
निग्रहो न च दण्डोऽस्ति न लोभो न परिग्रहः ॥ 49.115 ॥
1.49.m: There is no deceiver there, nor envy, nor thieves, nor fear; / there is neither restraint nor punishment, neither greed nor possessiveness.

1.49.s:
satyānṛtaṃ na tatrāsti dharmādharmau tathaiva ca.
varṇāśramāṇāṃ vārttā vā pāśupālyaṃ vaṇikkriyā .. 49.116 ..
1.49.d:
सत्यानृतं न तत्रास्ति धर्माधर्मौ तथैव च।
वर्णाश्रमाणां वार्त्ता वा पाशुपाल्यं वणिक्क्रिया ॥ 49.116 ॥
1.49.m: There is neither truth nor falsehood there, nor likewise virtue and vice, / nor any livelihood of the castes and life-stages, nor cattle-rearing, nor commercial trade.

1.49.s:
trayī vidyā daṇḍanītiḥ śuśrūṣā śalyameva ca.
varṣadvaye sarvametat puṣkarasya na vidyate .. 49.117 ..
1.49.d:
त्रयी विद्या दण्डनीतिः शुश्रूषा शल्यमेव च।
वर्षद्वये सर्वमेतत् पुष्करस्य न विद्यते ॥ 49.117 ॥
1.49.m: The three Vedas, the science of governance, service, and surgery— / all this is absent in the two realms of Puṣkara.

1.49.s:
na tatra nadyo varṣañca śītoṣṇaṃ vā na vidyate .
udbhijjānyudakānyatra giriprasravaṇāni ca .. 49.118 ..
1.49.d:
न तत्र नद्यो वर्षञ्च शीतोष्णं वा न विद्यते ।
उद्भिज्जान्युदकान्यत्र गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च ॥ 49.118 ॥
1.49.m: There are no rivers, nor rain, nor cold or heat there; / the waters there spring from the ground and from mountain streams.

1.49.s:
uttarāṇāṃ kurūṇāñca tulyakālo janaḥ sadā.
sarvatra susukhastatra jarāklamavivarjitaḥ .. 49.119 ..
1.49.d:
उत्तराणां कुरूणाञ्च तुल्यकालो जनः सदा।
सर्वत्र सुसुखस्तत्र जराक्लमविवर्जितः ॥ 49.119 ॥
1.49.m: The people there ever share the same lifespan as the northern Kurus; / they are completely happy everywhere, free from old age and fatigue.

1.49.s:
ityeṣa dhātakīkhaṇḍo mahāvīte tathaiva ca .
ānupūrvyādvidhiḥ kṛtsnaḥ puṣkarasya prakīrtitaḥ .. 49.120 ..
1.49.d:
इत्येष धातकीखण्डो महावीते तथैव च ।
आनुपूर्व्याद्विधिः कृत्स्नः पुष्करस्य प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 49.120 ॥
1.49.m: Thus the entire arrangement of Puṣkara, / in Dhātakīkhaṇḍa as well as in Mahāvīta, has been proclaimed in due order.

1.49.s:
svādūdakenodadhinā puṣkaraḥ parivāritaḥ.
vistarānmaṇḍalāccaiva puṣkarasya tathaiva ca .. 49.121 ..
1.49.d:
स्वादूदकेनोदधिना पुष्करः परिवारितः।
विस्तरान्मण्डलाच्चैव पुष्करस्य तथैव च ॥ 49.121 ॥
1.49.m: Puṣkara is surrounded by the ocean of fresh water, / which is equal to the breadth and circumference of Puṣkara.

1.49.s:
evaṃ dvīpāḥ samudraistu sapta saptabhirāvṛtāḥ.
dvīpasyānantaro yastu samudrastu samantataḥ .. 49.122 ..
1.49.d:
एवं द्वीपाः समुद्रैस्तु सप्त सप्तभिरावृताः।
द्वीपस्यानन्तरो यस्तु समुद्रस्तु समन्ततः ॥ 49.122 ॥
1.49.m: Thus the seven continents are enclosed by the seven oceans; / the ocean that is immediately contiguous to each continent surrounds it on all sides.

1.49.s:
evaṃ dvīpasamudrāṇāṃ vṛddhirjñeyā parasparāt.
apāñcaiva samudrekāt samudrā iti saṃjñitāḥ .. 49.123 ..
1.49.d:
एवं द्वीपसमुद्राणां वृद्धिर्ज्ञेया परस्परात्।
अपाञ्चैव समुद्रेकात् समुद्रा इति संज्ञिताः ॥ 49.123 ॥
1.49.m: Thus the increase of the continents and oceans from one to the next should be understood; / and because of the overflowing (*samudreka*) of waters, they are called oceans (*samudra*).

1.49.s:
ṛṣayo nivasantyasmin prajā yasmāccaturvidhāḥ.
tasmādvarṣamiti proktaṃ prajānāṃ sukhadantu tat .. 49.124 ..
1.49.d:
ऋषयो निवसन्त्यस्मिन् प्रजा यस्माच्चतुर्विधाः।
तस्माद्वर्षमिति प्रोक्तं प्रजानां सुखदन्तु तत् ॥ 49.124 ॥
1.49.m: Because the four classes of beings live (*ṛṣanti*) in it, / it is therefore called a realm (*varṣa*), and it bestows happiness upon beings.

1.49.s:
ṛṣa ityeva ṛṣayaḥ vṛṣaḥ śaktiprabandhane.
iti prabandhanāt siddhaṃ varṣatvaṃ tena teṣu tat .. 49.125 ..
1.49.d:
ऋष इत्येव ऋषयः वृषः शक्तिप्रबन्धने।
इति प्रबन्धनात् सिद्धं वर्षत्वं तेन तेषु तत् ॥ 49.125 ॥
1.49.m: *Ṛṣa* means seers (*ṛṣayaḥ*); *vṛṣa* means in the sense of binding power; / thus through binding, the nature of being a *varṣa* is established among them.

1.49.s:
śuklapakṣe candravṛddhau samudraḥ pūryate tadā.
prakṣīyamāṇe bahule kṣīyate'stamite khage .. 49.126 ..
1.49.d:
शुक्लपक्षे चन्द्रवृद्धौ समुद्रः पूर्यते तदा।
प्रक्षीयमाणे बहुले क्षीयतेऽस्तमिते खगे ॥ 49.126 ॥
1.49.m: In the bright fortnight, as the moon waxes, the ocean fills up; / in the waning dark [fortnight], as the sky-traveler sets, it diminishes.

1.49.s:
āpūryamāṇe udadhiḥ svata evābhipūryate.
tato'pakṣīyamāṇe'pi svātmanaivāpakṛṣyate .. 49.127 ..
1.49.d:
आपूर्यमाणे उदधिः स्वत एवाभिपूर्यते।
ततोऽपक्षीयमाणेऽपि स्वात्मनैवापकृष्यते ॥ 49.127 ॥
1.49.m: As it fills, the ocean swells of its own accord; / then, as it wanes, it is drawn back by itself alone.

1.49.s:
ukhāsthamagnisaṃyogāt jalamudricyate yathā.
tathā mahodadhigataṃ toyamudricyate tataḥ .. 49.128 ..
1.49.d:
उखास्थमग्निसंयोगात् जलमुद्रिच्यते यथा।
तथा महोदधिगतं तोयमुद्रिच्यते ततः ॥ 49.128 ॥
1.49.m: Just as water in a pot overflows from contact with fire, / so the water in the great ocean overflows from that [cause].

1.49.s:
anyūnāhyatiriktāśca varddhantyāpo hrasanti ca.
udayāstamitaiścendoḥ pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇayoḥ.
kṣayavṛddhirevamudadheḥ somavṛddhikṣayātpunaḥ .. 49.129 ..
1.49.d:
अन्यूनाह्यतिरिक्ताश्च वर्द्धन्त्यापो ह्रसन्ति च।
उदयास्तमितैश्चेन्दोः पक्षयोः शुक्लकृष्णयोः।
क्षयवृद्धिरेवमुदधेः सोमवृद्धिक्षयात्पुनः ॥ 49.129 ॥
1.49.m: Neither diminished nor augmented in total, the waters rise and fall / with the risings and settings of the moon in the bright and dark fortnights; / thus the decrease and increase of the ocean is caused by the waning and waxing of the moon.

1.49.s:
daśottarāṇi pañcaiva aṅgulīnāṃ śatāni tu.
apāṃ vṛddhiḥ kṣayo dṛṣṭaḥ samudrāṇāntu parvasu .. 49.130 ..
1.49.d:
दशोत्तराणि पञ्चैव अङ्गुलीनां शतानि तु।
अपां वृद्धिः क्षयो दृष्टः समुद्राणान्तु पर्वसु ॥ 49.130 ॥
1.49.m: An increase and decrease of five hundred and ten aṅgulas / of water in the oceans is observed on the junction-days.

1.49.s:
dvirāpatvāt smṛtā dvīpāḥ sarvataścodakāvṛtāḥ.
udakasyādhānaṃ yasmācca tasmādudadhirucyate .. 49.131 ..
1.49.d:
द्विरापत्वात् स्मृता द्वीपाः सर्वतश्चोदकावृताः।
उदकस्याधानं यस्माच्च तस्मादुदधिरुच्यते ॥ 49.131 ॥
1.49.m: Continents are called *dvīpa*s because of having water on two sides (*dvir-āpa*) and being surrounded by water on all sides; / and because it is the reservoir (*ādhāna*) of water (*udaka*), it is called *udadhi*.

1.49.s:
aparvāṇastu girayaḥ parvabhiḥ parvatāḥ smṛtāḥ .
plakṣadvīpe tu gomedaḥ parvatastena cocyate .. 49.132 ..
1.49.d:
अपर्वाणस्तु गिरयः पर्वभिः पर्वताः स्मृताः ।
प्लक्षद्वीपे तु गोमेदः पर्वतस्तेन चोच्यते ॥ 49.132 ॥
1.49.m: Hills have no joints, whereas mountains are called *parvata*s because of their joints (*parvan*); / in Plakṣadvīpa, Mount Gomeda is so called for that reason.

1.49.s:
śālmaliḥ śālmaladvīpe pūjyate ca mahādrumāḥ.
kuśadvīpe kuśastambastasya nāmnā sa ucyate .. 49.133 ..
1.49.d:
शाल्मलिः शाल्मलद्वीपे पूज्यते च महाद्रुमाः।
कुशद्वीपे कुशस्तम्बस्तस्य नाम्ना स उच्यते ॥ 49.133 ॥
1.49.m: On Śālmaladvīpa, the great Śālmali tree is worshiped; / on Kuśadvīpa there is a clump of Kuśa grass, after whose name it is called.

1.49.s:
krauñcadvīpe giriḥ krauñco madhye janapadasya ha.
śakadvīpe drumaḥ śākastasya nāmnā sa ucyate .. 49.134 ..
1.49.d:
क्रौञ्चद्वीपे गिरिः क्रौञ्चो मध्ये जनपदस्य ह।
शकद्वीपे द्रुमः शाकस्तस्य नाम्ना स उच्यते ॥ 49.134 ॥
1.49.m: On Krauñcadvīpa there is Mount Krauñca in the middle of the inhabited region; / on Śākadvīpa there is a Śāka tree, after whose name it is called.

1.49.s:
nyagrodhaḥ puṣkaradvīpe tatra taiḥ sa namaskṛtaḥ.
mahādevaḥ puṣkare tu brahmā tribhuvaneśvaraḥ .. 49.135 ..
1.49.d:
न्यग्रोधः पुष्करद्वीपे तत्र तैः स नमस्कृतः।
महादेवः पुष्करे तु ब्रह्मा त्रिभुवनेश्वरः ॥ 49.135 ॥
1.49.m: On Puṣkaradvīpa there is a Nyagrodha tree; there it is bowed down to by them. / On Puṣkara dwells the great god Brahmā, the lord of the three worlds.

1.49.s:
tasminnivasati brahmā sādhyaiḥ sārddhaṃ prajāpatiḥ.
upāsate tatra devāstrayastriṃśanmaharṣibhiḥ.
sa tatra pūjyate caiva devairdevottamottamaḥ .. 49.136 ..
1.49.d:
तस्मिन्निवसति ब्रह्मा साध्यैः सार्द्धं प्रजापतिः।
उपासते तत्र देवास्त्रयस्त्रिंशन्महर्षिभिः।
स तत्र पूज्यते चैव देवैर्देवोत्तमोत्तमः ॥ 49.136 ॥
1.49.m: On it Prajāpati Brahmā resides along with the Sādhyas; / the thirty-three gods together with the great seers worship him there; / he, the highest of the highest gods, is worshiped there by the gods.

1.49.s:
jambūdvīpātpravarttante ratnāni vividhāni ca.
dvīpeṣu teṣu sarveṣu prajānāṃ hi kramāstviha .. 49.137 ..
1.49.d:
जम्बूद्वीपात्प्रवर्त्तन्ते रत्नानि विविधानि च।
द्वीपेषु तेषु सर्वेषु प्रजानां हि क्रमास्त्विह ॥ 49.137 ॥
1.49.m: Various precious stones originate from Jambūdvīpa; / across all those continents, the stages of the peoples [advance] in regular order:

1.49.s:
sarvaso brahmacaryeṇa satyena ca damena ca.
ārogyāyuḥpramāṇāddhi dviguṇañca samantataḥ .. 49.138 ..
1.49.d:
सर्वसो ब्रह्मचर्येण सत्येन च दमेन च।
आरोग्यायुःप्रमाणाद्धि द्विगुणञ्च समन्ततः ॥ 49.138 ॥
1.49.m: wholly in chastity, truth, and self-restraint; / indeed, health and the measure of life double [from continent to continent] on every side.

1.49.s:
etasmin puṣkaradvīpe yaduktaṃ varṣakadvayam.
gopāyati prajāstatra svayaṃ sajjanamaṇḍitāḥ .. 49.139 ..
1.49.d:
एतस्मिन् पुष्करद्वीपे यदुक्तं वर्षकद्वयम्।
गोपायति प्रजास्तत्र स्वयं सज्जनमण्डिताः ॥ 49.139 ॥
1.49.m: In these two realms that have been spoken of on Puṣkaradvīpa, / [the Lord] himself protects the peoples adorned with virtuous men;

1.49.s:
īśvaro daṇḍamudyamya brahmā tribhuvaneśvaraḥ.
saviṣṇuḥ saśivo devaḥ sapitā sapitāmahaḥ .. 49.140 ..
1.49.d:
ईश्वरो दण्डमुद्यम्य ब्रह्मा त्रिभुवनेश्वरः।
सविष्णुः सशिवो देवः सपिता सपितामहः ॥ 49.140 ॥
1.49.m: the Lord Brahmā, ruler of the three worlds, raising his rod [of punishment], / accompanied by Viṣṇu and Śiva, the god who is the father and grandfather [of all].

1.49.s:
bhojanañcāprayatnena tatra svayamupasthitam .
ṣaḍrasaṃ sumahāvīryaṃ bhuñjate ca prajāḥ sadā .. 49.141 ..
1.49.d:
भोजनञ्चाप्रयत्नेन तत्र स्वयमुपस्थितम् ।
षड्रसं सुमहावीर्यं भुञ्जते च प्रजाः सदा ॥ 49.141 ॥
1.49.m: And food appears there of its own accord without effort, / endowed with the six tastes and exceedingly potent, which the people ever enjoy.

1.49.s:
pareṇa puṣkarasyātha āvṛtyā yaḥ sthito mahān .
svādūdakaḥ samudrastu samantātpariveṣṭitaḥ .. 49.142 ..
1.49.d:
परेण पुष्करस्याथ आवृत्या यः स्थितो महान् ।
स्वादूदकः समुद्रस्तु समन्तात्परिवेष्टितः ॥ 49.142 ॥
1.49.m: Beyond Puṣkara stands the great ocean of fresh water / which encloses it, encircling it on all sides.

1.49.s:
pareṇa tasya mahatī dṛśyate loka saṃsthitiḥ.
kāñcanī dviguṇā bhūmiḥ sarvā caikaśilopamā .. 49.143 ..
1.49.d:
परेण तस्य महती दृश्यते लोक संस्थितिः।
काञ्चनी द्विगुणा भूमिः सर्वा चैकशिलोपमा ॥ 49.143 ॥
1.49.m: Beyond that is seen the great constitution of the worlds: / a golden land, twice as wide, all resembling a single stone slab.

1.49.s:
tasmātpareṇa śailastu maryādānte tu maṇḍalam.
prakāśaścāprakāśaśca lokālokaḥ sa ucyate .. 49.144 ..
1.49.d:
तस्मात्परेण शैलस्तु मर्यादान्ते तु मण्डलम्।
प्रकाशश्चाप्रकाशश्च लोकालोकः स उच्यते ॥ 49.144 ॥
1.49.m: Beyond that is the mountain range that forms a circular boundary; / it is called Lokāloka, being both light and dark.

1.49.s:
ālokastasya cārvāktu nirālokastataḥ param.
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi daśa tasyocchrayaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 49.145 ..
1.49.d:
आलोकस्तस्य चार्वाक्तु निरालोकस्ततः परम्।
योजनानां सहस्राणि दश तस्योच्छ्रयः स्मृतः ॥ 49.145 ॥
1.49.m: On this side of it is light (*āloka*), and beyond it is darkness (*nirāloka*); / its height is recorded as ten thousand yojanas,

1.49.s:
tāvāṃśca vistarastasya pṛthivyāṃ kāmagaśca saḥ.
āloke lokaśabdastu nirāloke salokatā.
lokārthaṃ sammato loko nirālokastu bāhyataḥ .. 49.146 ..
1.49.d:
तावांश्च विस्तरस्तस्य पृथिव्यां कामगश्च सः।
आलोके लोकशब्दस्तु निरालोके सलोकता।
लोकार्थं सम्मतो लोको निरालोकस्तु बाह्यतः ॥ 49.146 ॥
1.49.m: and its width on the earth is just as much, moving at will. / In the light is the word *loka* [world], while in the darkness is [its opposite]; / the *loka* is recognized for the sake of the world, while the dark [realm] lies beyond.

1.49.s:
lokavistāramātrantu ālokaḥ sarvato bahiḥ.
paricchinnaḥ samantācca udakenāvṛtaśca saḥ.
nirālokātparaścāpi aṇḍamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati .. 49.147 ..
1.49.d:
लोकविस्तारमात्रन्तु आलोकः सर्वतो बहिः।
परिच्छिन्नः समन्ताच्च उदकेनावृतश्च सः।
निरालोकात्परश्चापि अण्डमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ 49.147 ॥
1.49.m: The realm of light extends as far as the world, everywhere on the outside; / it is bounded all around, and covered by water; / and beyond the realm of darkness it stands enveloping the cosmic egg.

1.49.s:
aṇḍasyāntastvime lokāḥ saptadvīpā ca medinī.
bhūrloko'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarloko'tha mahastathā .. 49.148 ..
1.49.d:
अण्डस्यान्तस्त्विमे लोकाः सप्तद्वीपा च मेदिनी।
भूर्लोकोऽथ भुवर्लोकः स्वर्लोकोऽथ महस्तथा ॥ 49.148 ॥
1.49.m: Within the cosmic egg are these worlds, and the earth with its seven continents: / Bhūrloka, then Bhuvarloka, Svarloka, and likewise Mahar[loka],

1.49.s:
janastapastathā satya etāvān lokasaṅ‌grahaḥ.
ekāvāneva vijñeyo lokāntaścaiva tatparaḥ .. 49.149 ..
1.49.d:
जनस्तपस्तथा सत्य एतावान् लोकसङ्‌ग्रहः।
एकावानेव विज्ञेयो लोकान्तश्चैव तत्परः ॥ 49.149 ॥
1.49.m: Janas, Tapas, and Satya—such is the collection of worlds. / The end of the worlds is to be understood as just so great, and beyond it is that [other realm].

1.49.s:
kumbasthāyī bhavedyādṛk pratīcyāndiśi candramāḥ.
āditaḥ śuklapakṣasya vapuraṇḍasya tadvidham .. 49.150 ..
1.49.d:
कुम्बस्थायी भवेद्यादृक् प्रतीच्यान्दिशि चन्द्रमाः।
आदितः शुक्लपक्षस्य वपुरण्डस्य तद्विधम् ॥ 49.150 ॥
1.49.m: Just as the moon, situated in the western quarter, appears like a water-jar / at the beginning of the bright fortnight, such is the form of the cosmic egg.

1.49.s:
aṇḍānāmīdṛśānāntu koṭyo jñeyāḥ sahasraśaḥ.
tiryagūrdhvamadhastācca kāraṇasyāvyayātmanaḥ.
kāraṇaiḥ prākṛtaistatra hyāvṛtaṃ pratisaptabhiḥ .. 49.151 ..
1.49.d:
अण्डानामीदृशानान्तु कोट्यो ज्ञेयाः सहस्रशः।
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधस्ताच्च कारणस्याव्ययात्मनः।
कारणैः प्राकृतैस्तत्र ह्यावृतं प्रतिसप्तभिः ॥ 49.151 ॥
1.49.m: Thousands of crores of such cosmic eggs are to be known, / sideways, above, and below, belonging to the immutable Cause; / there, it is enveloped in sevenfold layers by the elemental causal factors.

1.49.s:
daśādhikyena cānyonyaṃ dhārayanti parasparam.
parasparāvṛtāḥ sarve utpannāśca parasparāt .. 49.152 ..
1.49.d:
दशाधिक्येन चान्योन्यं धारयन्ति परस्परम्।
परस्परावृताः सर्वे उत्पन्नाश्च परस्परात् ॥ 49.152 ॥
1.49.m: Ten times greater in succession, they support one another; / they are all enveloped by one another and born from one another.

1.49.s:
aṇḍasyāsya samantāttu sanniviṣṭo ghanodadhiḥ.
samantādyena toyena dhāryamāṇaḥ sa tiṣṭhati .. 49.153 ..
1.49.d:
अण्डस्यास्य समन्तात्तु सन्निविष्टो घनोदधिः।
समन्ताद्येन तोयेन धार्यमाणः स तिष्ठति ॥ 49.153 ॥
1.49.m: All around this cosmic egg is situated the dense ocean; / it stands supported on all sides by that water.

1.49.s:
bāhyato ghanatoyasya tiryagūrddhvānumaṇḍalam.
dhāryamāṇaṃ samantāttu tiṣṭhate ghanatejasā .. 49.154 ..
1.49.d:
बाह्यतो घनतोयस्य तिर्यगूर्द्ध्वानुमण्डलम्।
धार्यमाणं समन्तात्तु तिष्ठते घनतेजसा ॥ 49.154 ॥
1.49.m: Outside the dense water, encircling it obliquely and above, / stands [the circle], supported all around by dense fire.

1.49.s:
ayoguḍanibho vahniḥ samantānmaṇḍalākṛtiḥ.
samantāddhanavātena dhāryamāṇaḥ sa tiṣṭhati.
ghanavātastathākāśandhārayāṇastu tiṣṭhati .. 49.155 ..
1.49.d:
अयोगुडनिभो वह्निः समन्तान्मण्डलाकृतिः।
समन्ताद्धनवातेन धार्यमाणः स तिष्ठति।
घनवातस्तथाकाशन्धारयाणस्तु तिष्ठति ॥ 49.155 ॥
1.49.m: The fire resembles an iron sphere, circular in shape all around; / it stands supported on all sides by dense wind; / and the dense wind stands supporting space.

1.49.s:
bhūtādiśca tathākāśaṃ bhūtādyañcāpyasau mahān .
mahān vyāpto hyanantena avyaktena tu dhāryate .. 49.156 ..
1.49.d:
भूतादिश्च तथाकाशं भूताद्यञ्चाप्यसौ महान् ।
महान् व्याप्तो ह्यनन्तेन अव्यक्तेन तु धार्यते ॥ 49.156 ॥
1.49.m: And the origin of the elements [supports] space, and that Mahat [supports] the origin of the elements; / Mahat, pervaded by the infinite, is supported by the Unmanifest.

1.49.s:
anantamaparivyaktandaśadhā sūkṣma eva ca.
anantamakṛtātmānamanādinidhanañca tat .. 49.157 ..
1.49.d:
अनन्तमपरिव्यक्तन्दशधा सूक्ष्म एव च।
अनन्तमकृतात्मानमनादिनिधनञ्च तत् ॥ 49.157 ॥
1.49.m: The infinite is completely manifest tenfold and subtle indeed; / that infinite is uncreated, without beginning and without end.

1.49.s:
atītya para to ghoramanālambamanāmayam.
naikayojanasāhasraṃ viprakṛṣṭaṃ tamovṛtam .. 49.158 ..
1.49.d:
अतीत्य पर तो घोरमनालम्बमनामयम्।
नैकयोजनसाहस्रं विप्रकृष्टं तमोवृतम् ॥ 49.158 ॥
1.49.m: Passing beyond it is the dreadful [realm], unsupported and free from affliction, / stretching over many thousands of yojanas, enveloped in darkness,

1.49.s:
tama eva nirālokamamaryādamadeśikam.
devānāmapyavidiṃtaṃ vyavahāravivarjjitam .. 49.159 ..
1.49.d:
तम एव निरालोकममर्यादमदेशिकम्।
देवानामप्यविदिंतं व्यवहारविवर्ज्जितम् ॥ 49.159 ॥
1.49.m: darkness alone, devoid of light, boundless, guide-less, / unknown even to the gods, free from worldly transaction.

1.49.s:
tamaso'nte ca vikhyātamākāśānte ca bhāsvaram.
maryādāyāmatastasya śivasyāyatanaṃ mahat .. 49.160 ..
1.49.d:
तमसोऽन्ते च विख्यातमाकाशान्ते च भास्वरम्।
मर्यादायामतस्तस्य शिवस्यायतनं महत् ॥ 49.160 ॥
1.49.m: At the end of the darkness, and at the end of space, radiant [and] renowned, / at the boundary of that, is the great abode of Śiva,

1.49.s:
tridaśānāmagamyantu sthānaṃ divyamiti śrutiḥ.
mahato devadevasya maryādāyāṃ vyavasthitam .. 49.161 ..
1.49.d:
त्रिदशानामगम्यन्तु स्थानं दिव्यमिति श्रुतिः।
महतो देवदेवस्य मर्यादायां व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 49.161 ॥
1.49.m: an inaccessible divine place for the gods—so states tradition; / it is situated on the boundary of the great God of gods.

1.49.s:
candrādityāvataptāstu ye lokāḥ prathitā budhaiḥ.
te lokā ityabhihitā jagataśca na saṃśayaḥ .. 49.162 ..
1.49.d:
चन्द्रादित्यावतप्तास्तु ये लोकाः प्रथिता बुधैः।
ते लोका इत्यभिहिता जगतश्च न संशयः ॥ 49.162 ॥
1.49.m: The worlds illuminated by the sun and moon are proclaimed by the wise; / those are called the worlds, and of the world there is no doubt.

1.49.s:
rasātalatalāt sapta saptaivorddhvatalāḥ kṣitau.
saptaskandhāstathā vāyoḥ sabrahmasadanā dvijāḥ .. 49.163 ..
1.49.d:
रसातलतलात् सप्त सप्तैवोर्द्ध्वतलाः क्षितौ।
सप्तस्कन्धास्तथा वायोः सब्रह्मसदना द्विजाः ॥ 49.163 ॥
1.49.m: From the surface of the netherworld there are seven [levels], and on the earth there are seven upper levels; / likewise, O twice-born, there are the seven layers of wind together with the abode of Brahmā.

1.49.s:
āpātālāddivaṃ yāvadatra pañcavidhā gatiḥ.
pramāṇametajjagata eṣa saṃsārasāgaraḥ .. 49.164 ..
1.49.d:
आपातालाद्दिवं यावदत्र पञ्चविधा गतिः।
प्रमाणमेतज्जगत एष संसारसागरः ॥ 49.164 ॥
1.49.m: From Pātāla up to heaven, fivefold is the course of destiny here; / this is the measure of the world; this is the ocean of the cycle of rebirth.

1.49.s:
anādyantā prayātyevaṃ naikajātisamudbhavāḥ.
vicitrā jagataḥ sā vai pravṛttiranavasthitā .. 49.165 ..
1.49.d:
अनाद्यन्ता प्रयात्येवं नैकजातिसमुद्भवाः।
विचित्रा जगतः सा वै प्रवृत्तिरनवस्थिता ॥ 49.165 ॥
1.49.m: Thus it proceeds without beginning or end, with births in many species; / manifold indeed is that unceasing course of worldly existence,

1.49.s:
yathaitad bhautikaṃ nāma nisargabahuvistaram.
atīndriyairmahābhāgaiḥ siddhairapi na lakṣyate .. 49.166 ..
1.49.d:
यथैतद् भौतिकं नाम निसर्गबहुविस्तरम्।
अतीन्द्रियैर्महाभागैः सिद्धैरपि न लक्ष्यते ॥ 49.166 ॥
1.49.m: just as this material creation, by nature vastly extended, / is not perceived even by the exalted siddhas who have transcended the senses.

1.49.s:
pṛthivyāñcāgnivāyūnāṃ mahatastamasastathā.
īśvarasya tu devasya anantasya dvijottamāḥ .. 49.167 ..
1.49.d:
पृथिव्याञ्चाग्निवायूनां महतस्तमसस्तथा।
ईश्वरस्य तु देवस्य अनन्तस्य द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 49.167 ॥
1.49.m: Of the earth, fire, and wind, and of the great [principle] and darkness, / as well as of the Lord, the infinite God, O best of the twice-born,

1.49.s:
kṣayo vā parimāṇaṃ vā anto vāpi na vidyate.
ananta eṣa sarvatra sarvasthāneṣu paṭhyate.
tasya coktaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ tasminnāmānukīrttane .. 49.168 ..
1.49.d:
क्षयो वा परिमाणं वा अन्तो वापि न विद्यते।
अनन्त एष सर्वत्र सर्वस्थानेषु पठ्यते।
तस्य चोक्तं मया पूर्वं तस्मिन्नामानुकीर्त्तने ॥ 49.168 ॥
1.49.m: there is no destruction, nor measure, nor end. / This infinite one is proclaimed everywhere, in all places; / and of Him it was told by me previously during the enumeration of names.

1.49.s:
ya eṣa śivanāmnā hi tadvaḥ kārtsnyena kīrtitam.
sa eṣa sarvatra gataḥ sarvasthāneṣu pūjyate .. 49.169 ..
1.49.d:
य एष शिवनाम्ना हि तद्वः कार्त्स्न्येन कीर्तितम्।
स एष सर्वत्र गतः सर्वस्थानेषु पूज्यते ॥ 49.169 ॥
1.49.m: He who is known by the name Śiva has been described to you in full; / that very one is omnipresent, worshipped in all places—

1.49.s:
bhūmau rasātale caiva ākāśe pavane'nale.
arṇaveṣu ca sarveṣu divi caiva na saṃśayaḥ .. 49.170 ..
1.49.d:
भूमौ रसातले चैव आकाशे पवनेऽनले।
अर्णवेषु च सर्वेषु दिवि चैव न संशयः ॥ 49.170 ॥
1.49.m: on earth, in the netherworld, in space, in the wind, in fire, / in all the oceans, and in heaven, without doubt.

1.49.s:
tathā tapasi vijñeya eṣa eva mahādyutiḥ.
anekadhā vibhaktāṅgo mahāyogī maheśvaraḥ.
sarvalokeṣu lokeśa ijyate bahudhā prabhuḥ .. 49.171 ..
1.49.d:
तथा तपसि विज्ञेय एष एव महाद्युतिः।
अनेकधा विभक्ताङ्गो महायोगी महेश्वरः।
सर्वलोकेषु लोकेश इज्यते बहुधा प्रभुः ॥ 49.171 ॥
1.49.m: Likewise, in austerity is this very one of great splendor to be recognized; / with limbs divided manifold, the great yogin Maheśvara, / the Lord of worlds, the Ruler, is worshipped in various ways in all worlds.

1.49.s:
evaṃ parasparotpannā dhāryante ca parasparān.
ādhārādheyabhāvena vikārāste vikāriṇaḥ .. 49.172 ..
1.49.d:
एवं परस्परोत्पन्ना धार्यन्ते च परस्परान्।
आधाराधेयभावेन विकारास्ते विकारिणः ॥ 49.172 ॥
1.49.m: Thus produced from one another, they are supported by one another; / through the relation of container and contained, those modifications belong to the modified.

1.49.s:
pṛthvyādayo vikārāste paricchinnāḥ parasparam.
parasparādhikāścaiva praviṣṭāśca parasparam .. 49.173 ..
1.49.d:
पृथ्व्यादयो विकारास्ते परिच्छिन्नाः परस्परम्।
परस्पराधिकाश्चैव प्रविष्टाश्च परस्परम् ॥ 49.173 ॥
1.49.m: Those modifications beginning with earth are bounded by one another, / each greater than the other, and entered into one another.

1.49.s:
yasmādviṣṭāśca te'nyonyaṃ tasmāt sthairyamupāgatāḥ.
prāgāsan hyaviśeṣāstu viśeṣānyonyaveśanāt.
pṛthivyādyāśca vāyvantāḥ paricchinnāstrayastu te .. 49.174 ..
1.49.d:
यस्माद्विष्टाश्च तेऽन्योन्यं तस्मात् स्थैर्यमुपागताः।
प्रागासन् ह्यविशेषास्तु विशेषान्योन्यवेशनात्।
पृथिव्याद्याश्च वाय्वन्ताः परिच्छिन्नास्त्रयस्तु ते ॥ 49.174 ॥
1.49.m: Because they have entered into one another, they have attained stability. / Formerly they were non-particularized, but through interpenetration they became particularized; / and those three beginning with earth and ending with wind are bounded.

1.49.s:
guṇāpacayasāreṇa paricchedo viśeṣataḥ.
śeṣāṇāṃ tu paricchedaḥ saukṣmyānneha vibhāvyate .. 49.175 ..
1.49.d:
गुणापचयसारेण परिच्छेदो विशेषतः।
शेषाणां तु परिच्छेदः सौक्ष्म्यान्नेह विभाव्यते ॥ 49.175 ॥
1.49.m: By virtue of the diminution of qualities, the boundary is distinct; / but the boundary of the remaining ones is not perceived here because of their subtlety.

1.49.s:
bhūtebhyaḥ paratastebhyo hyālokaḥ parataḥ smṛtaḥ.
bhūtānyāloka ākāśe paricchinnāni sarvaśaḥ .. 49.176 ..
1.49.d:
भूतेभ्यः परतस्तेभ्यो ह्यालोकः परतः स्मृतः।
भूतान्यालोक आकाशे परिच्छिन्नानि सर्वशः ॥ 49.176 ॥
1.49.m: Beyond those elements, light is recorded to be further; / the elements are bounded on all sides in light, [and light] in space.

1.49.s:
pātre mahati pātrāṇi yathaivāntargatāni tu.
bhavantyanyonyahīnāni parasparasamāśrayāt.
tathā hyāloka ākāśe bhedāstvantargatā matāḥ .. 49.177 ..
1.49.d:
पात्रे महति पात्राणि यथैवान्तर्गतानि तु।
भवन्त्यन्योन्यहीनानि परस्परसमाश्रयात्।
तथा ह्यालोक आकाशे भेदास्त्वन्तर्गता मताः ॥ 49.177 ॥
1.49.m: Just as vessels contained within a large vessel / are smaller than one another through mutual containment, / even so the divisions are considered contained within light and space.

1.49.s:
kṛtsnānyetāni catvāri anyonyasyādhikāni tu .
yāvadetāni bhūtāni tāvadutpatti rucyate .. 49.178 ..
1.49.d:
कृत्स्नान्येतानि चत्वारि अन्योन्यस्याधिकानि तु ।
यावदेतानि भूतानि तावदुत्पत्ति रुच्यते ॥ 49.178 ॥
1.49.m: All these four are progressively greater than one another; / as far as these elements extend, so far is creation spoken of.

1.49.s:
jantūnāmiha saṃskāro bhūteṣvantargato matāḥ.
pratyākhyāya ca bhūtāni kāryotpattirna vidyate .. 49.179 ..
1.49.d:
जन्तूनामिह संस्कारो भूतेष्वन्तर्गतो मताः।
प्रत्याख्याय च भूतानि कार्योत्पत्तिर्न विद्यते ॥ 49.179 ॥
1.49.m: The disposition of living beings here is considered contained within the elements; / without the elements, the production of an effect does not occur.

1.49.s:
tasmātparimitā bhedāḥ smṛtāḥ kāryātmakāstu te.
kāraṇātmakāstathaiva syurbhedā ye mahadādayaḥ .. 49.180 ..
1.49.d:
तस्मात्परिमिता भेदाः स्मृताः कार्यात्मकास्तु ते।
कारणात्मकास्तथैव स्युर्भेदा ये महदादयः ॥ 49.180 ॥
1.49.m: Therefore those divisions consisting of effects are recorded to be limited; / likewise, the divisions beginning with Mahat consist of causes.

1.49.s:
ityeṣa sanniveśo vo mayā prokto vibhāgaśaḥ.
saptadvīpasamudrāyā yāthātathyena vai dvijāḥ .. 49.181 ..
1.49.d:
इत्येष सन्निवेशो वो मया प्रोक्तो विभागशः।
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्राया याथातथ्येन वै द्विजाः ॥ 49.181 ॥
1.49.m: Thus this arrangement of the [earth] having seven continents and oceans / has been declared by me to you in detail according to the truth, O twice-born.

1.49.s:
vistārānmaṇjalāccaiva prasaṃkhyātena caiva hi .
vaiśvarūpaṃ pradhānasya parimāṇaikadeśikam .. 49.182 ..
1.49.d:
विस्तारान्मण्जलाच्चैव प्रसंख्यातेन चैव हि ।
वैश्वरूपं प्रधानस्य परिमाणैकदेशिकम् ॥ 49.182 ॥
1.49.m: By extent, by orb, and by computation, / the universal form of Pradhāna is described in a part of its measure,

1.49.s:
adiṣṭhānaṃ bhaganato yasya sarvamidaṃ jagat .
evaṃ bhūtagaṇāḥ sapta sanniviṣṭāḥ parasparam .. 49.183 ..
1.49.d:
अदिष्ठानं भगनतो यस्य सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
एवं भूतगणाः सप्त सन्निविष्टाः परस्परम् ॥ 49.183 ॥
1.49.m: the foundation of the Blessed One, to whom belongs this entire universe. / Thus the seven groups of elements are arranged mutually.

1.49.s:
etāvān sanniveśastu mayā śakyaḥ prabhāvitu m.
etāvadeva śrotavyaṃ sanniveśe tu pārthiva .. 49.184 ..
1.49.d:
एतावान् सन्निवेशस्तु मया शक्यः प्रभावितु म्।
एतावदेव श्रोतव्यं सन्निवेशे तु पार्थिव ॥ 49.184 ॥
1.49.m: Only this much of the arrangement can be explained by me; / only this much should be heard concerning the arrangement, O king.

1.49.s:
sapta prakṛtayastvetā dhārayanti parasparam.
tāsvalpaparimāṇena prasaṅkhyātumihocyate.
asaṅkhyeyāḥ prakṛtayastiryagūrddhvamadhaśca yāḥ .. 49.185 ..
1.49.d:
सप्त प्रकृतयस्त्वेता धारयन्ति परस्परम्।
तास्वल्पपरिमाणेन प्रसङ्ख्यातुमिहोच्यते।
असङ्ख्येयाः प्रकृतयस्तिर्यगूर्द्ध्वमधश्च याः ॥ 49.185 ॥
1.49.m: These seven cosmic principles support one another; / of them, an enumeration in small measure is spoken of here; / countless are the cosmic principles that exist obliquely, above, and below.

1.49.s:
tārakāsanniveśaśca yāvaddivyaṃ tu maṇjalam.
maryādāsanniveśastu bhūmestadanumaṇḍalam.
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi pṛthivyāṃ vai dvijottamāḥ .. 49.186 ..
1.49.d:
तारकासन्निवेशश्च यावद्दिव्यं तु मण्जलम्।
मर्यादासन्निवेशस्तु भूमेस्तदनुमण्डलम्।
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि पृथिव्यां वै द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 49.186 ॥
1.49.m: Such is the arrangement of stars as far as the celestial orb extends; / the arrangement of boundaries along the circle of the earth [is thus]. / Beyond this, I shall speak concerning the earth, O best of the twice-born.

1.49.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte bhuvanavinyāso nāmaikonapañcāśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 49 ..
1.49.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते भुवनविन्यासो नामैकोनपञ्चाशोऽध्यायः ॥ 49 ॥
1.49.m: Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, titled “The Arrangement of the Worlds,” in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.50.s:
..sūta uvāca..
adhaḥpramāṇamūrddhvañca varṇyamānaṃ nibodhata.
pṛthivī vāyurākāśamāpo jyotiśca pañcamam.
anantadhātavo hyete vyāpakāstu prakīrtitāḥ .. 50.1 ..
1.50.d:
॥सूत उवाच॥
अधःप्रमाणमूर्द्ध्वञ्च वर्ण्यमानं निबोधत।
पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्।
अनन्तधातवो ह्येते व्यापकास्तु प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 50.1 ॥
1.50.m:
The Sūta said:
Understand the measurement below and above as it is described.
Earth, wind, space, water, and fire as the fifth—
these are indeed proclaimed to be pervasive elements of infinite extent.

1.50.s:
jananī sarvabhūtānāṃ sarva bhūtadharā dharā.
nānājanapadākīrṇā nānādhiṣṭhānapattanā .. 50.2 ..
1.50.d:
जननी सर्वभूतानां सर्व भूतधरा धरा।
नानाजनपदाकीर्णा नानाधिष्ठानपत्तना ॥ 50.2 ॥
1.50.m:
The earth is the mother of all beings, bearing all beings,
thronged with various lands, with various settlements and cities,

1.50.s:
nānānadanadīśailā naikajātisamākulā.
anantā gīyate devī pṛthivī bahuvistarā .. 50.3 ..
1.50.d:
नानानदनदीशैला नैकजातिसमाकुला।
अनन्ता गीयते देवी पृथिवी बहुविस्तरा ॥ 50.3 ॥
1.50.m:
having various rivers, streams, and mountains, crowded with many species;
the goddess Earth of vast extent is sung of as infinite.

1.50.s:
nadīnadasamudrasthāstathā kṣudrāśrayāḥ sthitāḥ.
parvatākāśasaṃsthāśca antarbhūmigatāśca yāḥ .. 50.4 ..
1.50.d:
नदीनदसमुद्रस्थास्तथा क्षुद्राश्रयाः स्थिताः।
पर्वताकाशसंस्थाश्च अन्तर्भूमिगताश्च याः ॥ 50.4 ॥
1.50.m:
The waters that reside in rivers, streams, and oceans, as well as those in small reservoirs,
those situated on mountains and in the sky, and those gone underground—

1.50.s:
āpo'nantāśca vijñeyāstathāgniḥ sarvalaukikaḥ.
anantaḥ paṭhyate caiva vyāpakaḥ sarvasambhavaḥ .. 50.5 ..
1.50.d:
आपोऽनन्ताश्च विज्ञेयास्तथाग्निः सर्वलौकिकः।
अनन्तः पठ्यते चैव व्यापकः सर्वसम्भवः ॥ 50.5 ॥
1.50.m:
infinite are those waters to be known, and likewise the fire of all the worlds;
it is taught as infinite, all-pervading, and the source of everything.

1.50.s:
tathākāśamanālambaṃ ramyaṃ nānāśrayaṃ smṛtam.
anantaṃ prathitaṃ sarvaṃ vāyuścākāśasambhavaḥ .. 50.6 ..
1.50.d:
तथाकाशमनालम्बं रम्यं नानाश्रयं स्मृतम्।
अनन्तं प्रथितं सर्वं वायुश्चाकाशसम्भवः ॥ 50.6 ॥
1.50.m:
Likewise, space is remembered as supportless, delightful, the refuge of diverse things;
it is widely known as wholly infinite, and wind arises from space.

1.50.s:
āpaḥ pṛthivyāmudake pṛthivī copari sthitā.
ākāśañcāparamadhaḥ punarbhūmiḥ punarjjalam .. 50.7 ..
1.50.d:
आपः पृथिव्यामुदके पृथिवी चोपरि स्थिता।
आकाशञ्चापरमधः पुनर्भूमिः पुनर्ज्जलम् ॥ 50.7 ॥
1.50.m:
Water rests on earth, and earth rests above water;
and below is another space, then earth again, then water again.

1.50.s:
evamantamanantasya bhautikasya na vidyate.
purā surairabhihitaṃ niścitantu nibodhata .. 50.8 ..
1.50.d:
एवमन्तमनन्तस्य भौतिकस्य न विद्यते।
पुरा सुरैरभिहितं निश्चितन्तु निबोधत ॥ 50.8 ॥
1.50.m:
Thus there is no end to the infinite world of elements.
Understand the conclusion spoken of old by the gods:

1.50.s:
bhūmirjalamathākāśamiti jñeyā paramparā.
sthitireṣā tu vijñeyā saptame'smin rasātale .. 50.9 ..
1.50.d:
भूमिर्जलमथाकाशमिति ज्ञेया परम्परा।
स्थितिरेषा तु विज्ञेया सप्तमेऽस्मिन् रसातले ॥ 50.9 ॥
1.50.m:
Earth, water, and then space—this succession should be known.
This order is to be recognized across these seven underworlds.

1.50.s:
daśayojanasāhasramekabhaumaṃ rasātalam.
sādhubhiḥ parivikhyātamekaikaṃ bahuvistaram .. 50.10 ..
1.50.d:
दशयोजनसाहस्रमेकभौमं रसातलम्।
साधुभिः परिविख्यातमेकैकं बहुविस्तरम् ॥ 50.10 ॥
1.50.m:
Each realm of the underworld measures ten thousand yojanas,
celebrated by the virtuous, each one of vast extent:

1.50.s:
prathamamatalañcaiva sutalantu tataḥ param.
tataḥ parataraṃ vidyādvitalaṃ bahuvistaram .. 50.11 ..
1.50.d:
प्रथममतलञ्चैव सुतलन्तु ततः परम्।
ततः परतरं विद्याद्वितलं बहुविस्तरम् ॥ 50.11 ॥
1.50.m:
first Atala, and Sutala beyond that;
beyond that one should know Vitala of vast extent;

1.50.s:
tato gabhastalaṃ nāma parataśca mahātalam.
śrītalañca tataḥ prāhuḥ pātālaṃ saptamaṃsmṛtam .. 50.12 ..
1.50.d:
ततो गभस्तलं नाम परतश्च महातलम्।
श्रीतलञ्च ततः प्राहुः पातालं सप्तमंस्मृतम् ॥ 50.12 ॥
1.50.m:
then the one named Gabhastala, and beyond that Mahātala;
then they speak of Śrītala, and Pātāla is remembered as the seventh.

1.50.s:
kṛṣṇabhaumañca prathamaṃ bhūmibhāgañca kīrttitam.
pāṇḍubhaumaṃ dvitīyantu tṛtīyaṃ raktamṛttikam .. 50.13 ..
1.50.d:
कृष्णभौमञ्च प्रथमं भूमिभागञ्च कीर्त्तितम्।
पाण्डुभौमं द्वितीयन्तु तृतीयं रक्तमृत्तिकम् ॥ 50.13 ॥
1.50.m:
The first section of ground is proclaimed to have black soil;
the second has pale soil, and the third has red clay;

1.50.s:
pītabhaumañcaturthantu pañcamaṃ śarkarātalam.
ṣaṣṭhaṃ silāmayañcaiva sauvarṇaṃ saptamantalam .. 50.14 ..
1.50.d:
पीतभौमञ्चतुर्थन्तु पञ्चमं शर्करातलम्।
षष्ठं सिलामयञ्चैव सौवर्णं सप्तमन्तलम् ॥ 50.14 ॥
1.50.m:
the fourth has yellow soil, and the fifth has a gravelly floor;
the sixth is made of stone, and the seventh floor is golden.

1.50.s:
prathame tu tale khyātamasurendrasya mandiram.
namucerindraśatrorhi mahānādasya cālayam .. 50.15 ..
1.50.d:
प्रथमे तु तले ख्यातमसुरेन्द्रस्य मन्दिरम्।
नमुचेरिन्द्रशत्रोर्हि महानादस्य चालयम् ॥ 50.15 ॥
1.50.m:
In the first subterranean realm is known the mansion of the lord of asuras,
of Namuci, the enemy of Indra, and the dwelling of Mahānāda,

1.50.s:
purañca śaṅkukarṇasya kabandhasya ca mandiram.
niṣkulādasya ca puraṃ prahṛṣṭajanasaṅkulam .. 50.16 ..
1.50.d:
पुरञ्च शङ्कुकर्णस्य कबन्धस्य च मन्दिरम्।
निष्कुलादस्य च पुरं प्रहृष्टजनसङ्कुलम् ॥ 50.16 ॥
1.50.m:
the city of Śaṅkukarṇa, and the mansion of Kabandha,
and the city of Niṣkulāda, crowded with joyous people,

1.50.s:
rākṣasasya ca bhīmasya śūladantasya cālayam.
lohitākṣakaliṅgānāṃ nagaraṃ śvāpadasya tu .. 50.17 ..
1.50.d:
राक्षसस्य च भीमस्य शूलदन्तस्य चालयम्।
लोहिताक्षकलिङ्गानां नगरं श्वापदस्य तु ॥ 50.17 ॥
1.50.m:
the dwelling of the terrible rākṣasa Śūladanta,
and the city of the Lohitākṣas, the Kaliṅgas, and of Śvāpada,

1.50.s:
dhanañjayasya ca puraṃ māhendrasya mahātmanaḥ .
kāliyasya ca nāgasya nagaraṃ kalasasya ca .. 50.18 ..
1.50.d:
धनञ्जयस्य च पुरं माहेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः ।
कालियस्य च नागस्य नगरं कलसस्य च ॥ 50.18 ॥
1.50.m:
the city of Dhanañjaya, of the great Māhendra,
and the city of the nāga Kāliya, and of Kalasa.

1.50.s:
evaṃ purasahasrāṇiṃ nāgadānavarakṣasām.
tale jñeyāni prathame kṛṣṇabhaume na saṃśayaḥ .. 50.19 ..
1.50.d:
एवं पुरसहस्राणिं नागदानवरक्षसाम्।
तले ज्ञेयानि प्रथमे कृष्णभौमे न संशयः ॥ 50.19 ॥
1.50.m:
Thus thousands of cities belonging to nāgas, dānavas, and rakṣases
are to be known without doubt in the first realm, having black soil.

1.50.s:
dvitīye'pi tale viprā daityendrasya surakṣasaḥ.
mahājambhasya ca tathā nagaraṃ prathamasya tu .. 50.20 ..
1.50.d:
द्वितीयेऽपि तले विप्रा दैत्येन्द्रस्य सुरक्षसः।
महाजम्भस्य च तथा नगरं प्रथमस्य तु ॥ 50.20 ॥
1.50.m:
In the second realm also, O Brahmins, is the city of the lord of daityas, Surakṣas,
and likewise the city of Mahājambha the foremost,

1.50.s:
hayagrīvasya kṛṣṇasya nikumbhasya ca mandiram.
śaṅkhākhyeyasya ca puraṃ nagaraṃ gomukhasya ca .. 50.21 ..
1.50.d:
हयग्रीवस्य कृष्णस्य निकुम्भस्य च मन्दिरम्।
शङ्खाख्येयस्य च पुरं नगरं गोमुखस्य च ॥ 50.21 ॥
1.50.m:
the mansion of Hayagrīva, of Kṛṣṇa, and of Nikumbha,
and the city of the one named Śaṅkha, and the city of Gomukha,

1.50.s:
rākṣasasya ca nīlasya meghasya krathanasya ca.
purañca kurupādasya mahoṣṇīṣasya cālayam .. 50.22 ..
1.50.d:
राक्षसस्य च नीलस्य मेघस्य क्रथनस्य च।
पुरञ्च कुरुपादस्य महोष्णीषस्य चालयम् ॥ 50.22 ॥
1.50.m:
of the rākṣasa Nīla, of Megha, and of Krathana,
and the city of Kurupāda, and the dwelling of Mahoṣṇīṣa,

1.50.s:
kambalasya ca nāgasya puramaśvatarasya ca.
kadruputrasya ca puraṃ takṣakasya mahātmanaḥ .. 50.23 ..
1.50.d:
कम्बलस्य च नागस्य पुरमश्वतरस्य च।
कद्रुपुत्रस्य च पुरं तक्षकस्य महात्मनः ॥ 50.23 ॥
1.50.m:
and the city of the nāga Kambala, and of Aśvatara,
and the city of Kadrū's son, the great Takṣaka.

1.50.s:
evaṃ purasahasrāṇi nāgadānavarakṣasām.
dvitīye'smin tale viprāḥ pāṇḍubhaume na saṃśayaḥ .. 50.24 ..
1.50.d:
एवं पुरसहस्राणि नागदानवरक्षसाम्।
द्वितीयेऽस्मिन् तले विप्राः पाण्डुभौमे न संशयः ॥ 50.24 ॥
1.50.m:
Thus thousands of cities belonging to nāgas, dānavas, and rakṣases
are in this second realm, having pale soil, O Brahmins, without doubt.

1.50.s:
tṛtīye tu talekhyātaṃ prahlādasya mahātmanaḥ.
anuhlādasya ca puraṃ detyendrasya mahātmanaḥ .. 50.25 ..
1.50.d:
तृतीये तु तलेख्यातं प्रह्लादस्य महात्मनः।
अनुह्लादस्य च पुरं देत्येन्द्रस्य महात्मनः ॥ 50.25 ॥
1.50.m:
In the third realm is known [the city] of the great Prahlāda,
and the city of Anuhlāda, the great lord of daityas,

1.50.s:
tārakākh‌yasya ca puraṃ puraṃ triśirasastathā.
śiśumārasya ca puraṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākulam .. 50.26 ..
1.50.d:
तारकाख्‌यस्य च पुरं पुरं त्रिशिरसस्तथा।
शिशुमारस्य च पुरं हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलम् ॥ 50.26 ॥
1.50.m:
and the city named after Tāraka, and likewise the city of Triśiras,
and the city of Śiśumāra, crowded with joyful and thriving people,

1.50.s:
cyavanasya ca vijñeyaṃ rākṣasasya ca mandiram.
rākṣasendrasya ca puraṃkumbhilasya kharasyaca .. 50.27 ..
1.50.d:
च्यवनस्य च विज्ञेयं राक्षसस्य च मन्दिरम्।
राक्षसेन्द्रस्य च पुरंकुम्भिलस्य खरस्यच ॥ 50.27 ॥
1.50.m:
and the mansion of the rākṣasa Cyavana is to be known,
and the city of the lord of rākṣasas Kumbhila, and of Khara,

1.50.s:
virādhasya ca krūrasya puramulkāmukhasya ca.
hemakasya ca nāgasya tathā pāṇḍurakasya ca .. 50.28 ..
1.50.d:
विराधस्य च क्रूरस्य पुरमुल्कामुखस्य च।
हेमकस्य च नागस्य तथा पाण्डुरकस्य च ॥ 50.28 ॥
1.50.m:
and the city of the cruel Virādha, and of Ulkāmukha,
and of the nāga Hemaka, and likewise of Pāṇḍuraka,

1.50.s:
maṇimantrasya ca puraṃ kapilasya ca mandiram.
nandasya coragapaterviśālasya ca mandiram .. 50.29 ..
1.50.d:
मणिमन्त्रस्य च पुरं कपिलस्य च मन्दिरम्।
नन्दस्य चोरगपतेर्विशालस्य च मन्दिरम् ॥ 50.29 ॥
1.50.m:
and the city of Maṇimantra, and the mansion of Kapila,
and the mansion of Nanda, the lord of uragas, and of Viśāla.

1.50.s:
evaṃ purasahasrāṇi nāgadānavarakṣasām.
tṛtīye'smistale viprāḥ pītabhaume na saṃśayaḥ .. 50.30 ..
1.50.d:
एवं पुरसहस्राणि नागदानवरक्षसाम्।
तृतीयेऽस्मिस्तले विप्राः पीतभौमे न संशयः ॥ 50.30 ॥
1.50.m:
Thus thousands of cities belonging to nāgas, dānavas, and rakṣases
are in this third realm, having yellow soil, O Brahmins, without doubt.

1.50.s:
caturthe daityasiṃhasya kālanemermahātmanaḥ.
gajakarṇasya ca puraṃ nagaraṃ kuñjarasya ca .. 50.31 ..
1.50.d:
चतुर्थे दैत्यसिंहस्य कालनेमेर्महात्मनः।
गजकर्णस्य च पुरं नगरं कुञ्जरस्य च ॥ 50.31 ॥
1.50.m:
In the fourth [realm is the city] of the lion of daityas, the great Kālanemi,
and the city of Gajakarṇa, and the city of Kuñjara,

1.50.s:
rākṣasendrasya ca puraṃ sumālerbahuvistaram.
muñjasya lokanāthasya vṛkavaktrasya cālayam .. 50.32 ..
1.50.d:
राक्षसेन्द्रस्य च पुरं सुमालेर्बहुविस्तरम्।
मुञ्जस्य लोकनाथस्य वृकवक्त्रस्य चालयम् ॥ 50.32 ॥
1.50.m:
and the city of vast extent belonging to Sumālin, the lord of rākṣasas,
and the dwelling of Muñja, the protector of the world, and of Vṛkavaktra;

1.50.s:
bahuyojanasāhasraṃ bahupakṣisamākulam .
nagaraṃ vainateyasya caturthe'smin rasātale .. 50.33 ..
1.50.d:
बहुयोजनसाहस्रं बहुपक्षिसमाकुलम् ।
नगरं वैनतेयस्य चतुर्थेऽस्मिन् रसातले ॥ 50.33 ॥
1.50.m:
extending for many thousands of yojanas, filled with many birds,
is the city of Vainateya in this fourth underworld.

1.50.s:
pañcame śarkarābhaume bahuyojanavistṛte.
virocanasya nagaraṃ daityasiṃhasya dhīmataḥ .. 50.34 ..
1.50.d:
पञ्चमे शर्कराभौमे बहुयोजनविस्तृते।
विरोचनस्य नगरं दैत्यसिंहस्य धीमतः ॥ 50.34 ॥
1.50.m:
In the fifth realm, with gravelly soil, extending for many yojanas,
is the city of Virocana, the wise lion of daityas,

1.50.s:
vaiḍhūryyasyāgnijihvasya hiraṇyākṣasya cālayam.
purañca vidyujjihvasya rākṣasasya ca dhīmataḥ .. 50.35 ..
1.50.d:
वैढूर्य्यस्याग्निजिह्वस्य हिरण्याक्षस्य चालयम्।
पुरञ्च विद्युज्जिह्वस्य राक्षसस्य च धीमतः ॥ 50.35 ॥
1.50.m:
and the dwelling of Vaiḍūrya, of Agnijihva, and of Hiraṇyākṣa,
and the city of the wise rākṣasa Vidyujjihva,

1.50.s:
mahāmeghasya ca puraṃ rākṣasendrasya śālinaḥ.
karmmārasya ca nāgasya svastikasya jayasya ca .. 50.36 ..
1.50.d:
महामेघस्य च पुरं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य शालिनः।
कर्म्मारस्य च नागस्य स्वस्तिकस्य जयस्य च ॥ 50.36 ॥
1.50.m:
and the city of Mahāmegha, the splendid lord of rākṣasas,
and of the nāga Karmāra, of Svastika, and of Jaya.

1.50.s:
evaṃ purasahasrāṇi nāgadānavarakṣasām.
pañcame'pi tathā jñeyaṃ śarkarānilaye sadā .. 50.37 ..
1.50.d:
एवं पुरसहस्राणि नागदानवरक्षसाम्।
पञ्चमेऽपि तथा ज्ञेयं शर्करानिलये सदा ॥ 50.37 ॥
1.50.m:
Thus thousands of cities belonging to nāgas, dānavas, and rakṣases
are to be known always in the fifth as well, in that gravelly abode.

1.50.s:
ṣaṣṭhe tale daityapateḥ kesarernagarottamam.
suparvvaṇaḥ sulomnaśca nagaraṃ mahiṣasya ca.
rākṣasendrasya ca puramutkrośasya mahātmanaḥ .. 50.38 ..
1.50.d:
षष्ठे तले दैत्यपतेः केसरेर्नगरोत्तमम्।
सुपर्व्वणः सुलोम्नश्च नगरं महिषस्य च।
राक्षसेन्द्रस्य च पुरमुत्क्रोशस्य महात्मनः ॥ 50.38 ॥
1.50.m:
In the sixth realm is the excellent city of the lord of daityas, Kesarin,
and the city of Suparvan, of Suloman, and of Mahiṣa,
and the city of the great lord of rākṣasas Utkrośa.

1.50.s:
tatrāste surasāputraḥ śataśīrṣo mudā yutaḥ.
kaśyapasya sutaḥ śrīmān vāsukirnāma nāgarāṭ .. 50.39 ..
1.50.d:
तत्रास्ते सुरसापुत्रः शतशीर्षो मुदा युतः।
कश्यपस्य सुतः श्रीमान् वासुकिर्नाम नागराट् ॥ 50.39 ॥
1.50.m:
There dwells the son of Surasā, hundred-headed, filled with joy,
the glorious son of Kaśyapa named Vāsuki, the king of nāgas.

1.50.s:
evaṃ purasahasrāṇi nāgadānavarakṣasām .
ṣaṣṭhe tale'smin vikhyāte śilābhaume rasātale .. 50.40 ..
1.50.d:
एवं पुरसहस्राणि नागदानवरक्षसाम् ।
षष्ठे तलेऽस्मिन् विख्याते शिलाभौमे रसातले ॥ 50.40 ॥
1.50.m:
Thus thousands of cities belonging to nāgas, dānavas, and rakṣases
are in this renowned sixth realm of the underworld, with stony soil.

1.50.s:
saptame tu tale jñeyaṃ pātāle sarvvapaścime .
puraṃ baleḥ pramuditaṃ naranārīsamākulam .. 50.41 ..
1.50.d:
सप्तमे तु तले ज्ञेयं पाताले सर्व्वपश्चिमे ।
पुरं बलेः प्रमुदितं नरनारीसमाकुलम् ॥ 50.41 ॥
1.50.m:
In the seventh realm, in Pātāla, the westernmost of all, should be known
the joyful city of Bali, crowded with men and women,

1.50.s:
asurāśīviṣaiḥ pūrṇamuddhṛtairddevaśatrubhiḥ.
mucukundasya daityasya tatra vai nagaraṃ mahat .. 50.42 ..
1.50.d:
असुराशीविषैः पूर्णमुद्धृतैर्द्देवशत्रुभिः।
मुचुकुन्दस्य दैत्यस्य तत्र वै नगरं महत् ॥ 50.42 ॥
1.50.m:
filled with venomous serpents of the asuras, haughty enemies of the gods;
there indeed is the great city of the daitya Mucukunda,

1.50.s:
anekairditiputrāṇāṃ samudīrṇairmahāpuraiḥ.
tathaiva nāganagaraiṛddhimadbhiḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 50.43 ..
1.50.d:
अनेकैर्दितिपुत्राणां समुदीर्णैर्महापुरैः।
तथैव नागनगरैऋद्धिमद्भिः सहस्रशः ॥ 50.43 ॥
1.50.m:
crowded with many rising great cities of the sons of Diti,
as well as with prosperous cities of the nāgas by the thousands,

1.50.s:
daityānāṃ dānavānāñca samudīrṇai rmahāpuraiḥ.
udīrṇai rākṣasāvāsairanekaiśca samākulam .. 50.44 ..
1.50.d:
दैत्यानां दानवानाञ्च समुदीर्णै र्महापुरैः।
उदीर्णै राक्षसावासैरनेकैश्च समाकुलम् ॥ 50.44 ॥
1.50.m:
with towering great cities of daityas and dānavas,
and with many lofty habitations of rākṣasas.

1.50.s:
pātālānte ca viprendrā vistīrṇe bahuyojane.
āste raktāravindākṣo mahātmā hyajarāmaraḥ .. 50.45 ..
1.50.d:
पातालान्ते च विप्रेन्द्रा विस्तीर्णे बहुयोजने।
आस्ते रक्तारविन्दाक्षो महात्मा ह्यजरामरः ॥ 50.45 ॥
1.50.m: And at the end of Pātāla, O best of Brahmins, extending over many yojanas, / dwells the great-souled one with eyes like red lotuses, ageless and immortal,

1.50.s:
dhautaśaṅkhodaravapurnīlavāsā mahābhujaḥ.
viśālabhogo dyutimāṃścitramālādharo balī .. 50.46 ..
1.50.d:
धौतशङ्खोदरवपुर्नीलवासा महाभुजः।
विशालभोगो द्युतिमांश्चित्रमालाधरो बली ॥ 50.46 ॥
1.50.m: having a body resembling the interior of a polished conch shell, clad in blue robes, long-armed, / with an immense hood, radiant, wearing a variegated garland, and mighty.

1.50.s:
rukmaśrṛṅagāvadātena dīptāsyena virājatā.
prabhurmukhasahasreṇa śobhate vai sa kuṇḍalī .. 50.47 ..
1.50.d:
रुक्मश्रृङगावदातेन दीप्तास्येन विराजता।
प्रभुर्मुखसहस्रेण शोभते वै स कुण्डली ॥ 50.47 ॥
1.50.m: Shining with radiance bright as golden horns, with radiant faces, / the lord gleams with his thousand heads, adorned with earrings.

1.50.s:
sa jihvāmālayā devo lolajvālānalārciṣā.
jvālāmālāparikṣiptaḥ kailāsa iva lakṣyate .. 50.48 ..
1.50.d:
स जिह्वामालया देवो लोलज्वालानलार्चिषा।
ज्वालामालापरिक्षिप्तः कैलास इव लक्ष्यते ॥ 50.48 ॥
1.50.m: With his garland of tongues, having the flare of flickering blazing fire, / that god looks like Mount Kailāsa enveloped in a garland of flames.

1.50.s:
sa tu netrasahasreṇa dviguṇena virājatā.
bālasūryyābhitāmreṇa śobhate snigdhamaṇḍalaḥ .. 50.49 ..
1.50.d:
स तु नेत्रसहस्रेण द्विगुणेन विराजता।
बालसूर्य्याभिताम्रेण शोभते स्निग्धमण्डलः ॥ 50.49 ॥
1.50.m: Indeed, shining with twice a thousand eyes, / deep red as the morning sun, his smooth body shines.

1.50.s:
tasya kundenduvarṇasya akṣamālā virājate .
taruṇādityamāleva śvetaparvvatamūrddhani .. 50.50 ..
1.50.d:
तस्य कुन्देन्दुवर्णस्य अक्षमाला विराजते ।
तरुणादित्यमालेव श्वेतपर्व्वतमूर्द्धनि ॥ 50.50 ॥
1.50.m: His garland of beads, white as jasmine and the moon, shines forth / like a garland of young suns upon the summit of a white mountain.

1.50.s:
jaṭākarālo dyutimān lakṣyate śayanāsane.
vistīrṇa iva medinyāṃ sahasraśikharo giriḥ .. 50.51 ..
1.50.d:
जटाकरालो द्युतिमान् लक्ष्यते शयनासने।
विस्तीर्ण इव मेदिन्यां सहस्रशिखरो गिरिः ॥ 50.51 ॥
1.50.m: Fierce with matted hair, radiant, he is seen upon his couch, / like a mountain with a thousand peaks spread out upon the earth.

1.50.s:
mahābhogairmahābhāgairmahānāgairmahābalaiḥ.
upāsyate mahātejā mahānāgapatiḥ svayam .. 50.52 ..
1.50.d:
महाभोगैर्महाभागैर्महानागैर्महाबलैः।
उपास्यते महातेजा महानागपतिः स्वयम् ॥ 50.52 ॥
1.50.m: Attended by mighty, fortunate, great serpents of immense power, / the intensely brilliant king of great serpents himself is worshiped.

1.50.s:
sa rājā sarvanāgānāṃ śeṣo nāma mahādyutiḥ.
sā vaiṣṇavī hyahitanurmaryādāyāṃ vyavasthitā .. 50.53 ..
1.50.d:
स राजा सर्वनागानां शेषो नाम महाद्युतिः।
सा वैष्णवी ह्यहितनुर्मर्यादायां व्यवस्थिता ॥ 50.53 ॥
1.50.m: He is the king of all serpents, named Śeṣa, of great splendour. / He is indeed the serpentine body of Viṣṇu established at the boundary.

1.50.s:
saptaivamete kathitā vyavahāryā rasātalāḥ .
devāsuramahānāgarākṣasādhyuṣitāḥ sadā .. 50.54 ..
1.50.d:
सप्तैवमेते कथिता व्यवहार्या रसातलाः ।
देवासुरमहानागराक्षसाध्युषिताः सदा ॥ 50.54 ॥
1.50.m: Thus these seven subterranean regions that can be experienced have been related, / perpetually inhabited by gods, asuras, great serpents, and rākṣasas.

1.50.s:
ataḥparamanālokyamagamyaṃ siddhasādhubhiḥ.
devā mānapyaviditaṃ vyavahāravivarjjitam .. 50.55 ..
1.50.d:
अतःपरमनालोक्यमगम्यं सिद्धसाधुभिः।
देवा मानप्यविदितं व्यवहारविवर्ज्जितम् ॥ 50.55 ॥
1.50.m: Beyond this, it is invisible, inaccessible to perfected beings and holy persons, / unknown even to the gods, and devoid of transactional activity.

1.50.s:
pṛthivyagnyambuvāyūnāṃ nabhasaśca dvijottamāḥ.
mahattvamevamṛṣibhirvarṇyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 50.56 ..
1.50.d:
पृथिव्यग्न्यम्बुवायूनां नभसश्च द्विजोत्तमाः।
महत्त्वमेवमृषिभिर्वर्ण्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ 50.56 ॥
1.50.m: The greatness of earth, fire, water, wind, / and sky, O best of the twice-born, is described in this way by the seers; there is no doubt in this.

1.50.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi sūryācandramasorgatim.
sūryācandramasāvetau bhramantau yāvadeva tu.
prakāśataḥ svabhābhistau maṇḍalābhyāṃ samāsthitau .. 50.57 ..
1.50.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि सूर्याचन्द्रमसोर्गतिम्।
सूर्याचन्द्रमसावेतौ भ्रमन्तौ यावदेव तु।
प्रकाशतः स्वभाभिस्तौ मण्डलाभ्यां समास्थितौ ॥ 50.57 ॥
1.50.m: Henceforth, I shall proclaim the course of the sun and the moon. / To the extent that the sun and the moon, wandering, / illuminate with their own splendours, stationed in their discs,

1.50.s:
saptānāñca samudrāṇāṃ dvīpānāntu sa vistaraḥ.
vistarārddhaṃ pṛthivyāstu bhavedanyatra bāhyataḥ .. 50.58 ..
1.50.d:
सप्तानाञ्च समुद्राणां द्वीपानान्तु स विस्तरः।
विस्तरार्द्धं पृथिव्यास्तु भवेदन्यत्र बाह्यतः ॥ 50.58 ॥
1.50.m: that is the extent of the seven oceans and continents. / Half the extent of the earth lies beyond, outside.

1.50.s:
paryāsapārimāṇyantu cāndrādityau prakāśataḥ.
paryāsapārimāṇyena bhūmestulyaṃ divaṃ smṛtam .. 50.59 ..
1.50.d:
पर्यासपारिमाण्यन्तु चान्द्रादित्यौ प्रकाशतः।
पर्यासपारिमाण्येन भूमेस्तुल्यं दिवं स्मृतम् ॥ 50.59 ॥
1.50.m: The sun and moon shine according to the circumference of their orbits. / Heaven is considered equal to the earth in the measure of its circumference.

1.50.s:
avati trīnimān lokān yasmāt sūryaḥ paribhraman.
avadhātuḥ prakāśākhyo hyavanātsa raviḥ smṛtaḥ .. 50.60 ..
1.50.d:
अवति त्रीनिमान् लोकान् यस्मात् सूर्यः परिभ्रमन्।
अवधातुः प्रकाशाख्यो ह्यवनात्स रविः स्मृतः ॥ 50.60 ॥
1.50.m: Because the sun, wandering around, protects these three worlds, / and the root *av* means to illuminate, from that protection he is called Ravi.

1.50.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi pramāṇaṃ candrasūryayoḥ.
mahitatvānmahīśabdo hyasmin varṣe nipātyate .. 50.61 ..
1.50.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रमाणं चन्द्रसूर्ययोः।
महितत्वान्महीशब्दो ह्यस्मिन् वर्षे निपात्यते ॥ 50.61 ॥
1.50.m: Henceforth, I shall describe the dimensions of the moon and the sun. / Because of its greatness, the word *mahī* is applied to this continent.

1.50.s:
asya bhāratavarṣasya viṣkambhantu suvistaram.
maṇḍalaṃ bhāskarasyātha yojanānāṃ nibodhata .. 50.62 ..
1.50.d:
अस्य भारतवर्षस्य विष्कम्भन्तु सुविस्तरम्।
मण्डलं भास्करस्याथ योजनानां निबोधत ॥ 50.62 ॥
1.50.m: Learn now the extensive diameter of this Bhāratavarṣa, / and the disc of the sun in yojanas.

1.50.s:
navayojanasāhasro vistāro bhāskarasya tu.
vistārātrriguṇaścāsya pariṇāho'tha maṇḍalam.
viṣkambo maṇjalasyaiva bhāskarād dviguṇaḥ śaśī .. 50.63 ..
1.50.d:
नवयोजनसाहस्रो विस्तारो भास्करस्य तु।
विस्तारात्र्रिगुणश्चास्य परिणाहोऽथ मण्डलम्।
विष्कम्बो मण्जलस्यैव भास्कराद् द्विगुणः शशी ॥ 50.63 ॥
1.50.m: The diameter of the sun is nine thousand yojanas; / its circumference, the disc, is thrice its diameter; / and the diameter of the disc of the moon is twice that of the sun.

1.50.s:
ataḥ pṛthivyāṃ vakṣyāmi pramāṇaṃ yojanaiḥ saha.
saptadvīpasamudrāyā vistāro maṇjalañca yat .. 50.64 ..
1.50.d:
अतः पृथिव्यां वक्ष्यामि प्रमाणं योजनैः सह।
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्राया विस्तारो मण्जलञ्च यत् ॥ 50.64 ॥
1.50.m: Hereafter I shall describe the dimensions on earth in yojanas, / the diameter and the circular extent of the earth with its seven continents and oceans.

1.50.s:
ityetadiha saṅkhyātaṃ purāṇaṃ parimāṇataḥ.
tadvakṣyāmi prasaṅkhyāya sāmpratairabhimānibhiḥ .. 50.65 ..
1.50.d:
इत्येतदिह सङ्ख्यातं पुराणं परिमाणतः।
तद्वक्ष्यामि प्रसङ्ख्याय साम्प्रतैरभिमानिभिः ॥ 50.65 ॥
1.50.m: Thus this Purāṇa has been calculated here in terms of measurement. / I shall explain that having calculated it through the presiding deities of the present.

1.50.s:
abhimānivyatītā ye tulyāste sāmpratairiha.
devā ye vai hyatītāste rūpairnāmabhireva ca .. 50.66 ..
1.50.d:
अभिमानिव्यतीता ये तुल्यास्ते साम्प्रतैरिह।
देवा ये वै ह्यतीतास्ते रूपैर्नामभिरेव च ॥ 50.66 ॥
1.50.m: Those past presiding deities were equal to the present ones here; / the gods who have passed were indeed [equal] in forms and in names.

1.50.s:
tasmāttu sāmpratairdevairvakṣyāmi vasudhātalam.
divastu sanniveśo vai sāmprataireva kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 50.67 ..
1.50.d:
तस्मात्तु साम्प्रतैर्देवैर्वक्ष्यामि वसुधातलम्।
दिवस्तु सन्निवेशो वै साम्प्रतैरेव कृत्स्नशः ॥ 50.67 ॥
1.50.m: Therefore, through the present gods I shall describe the surface of the earth, / and the entire layout of heaven through the present ones alone.

1.50.s:
śatārddha koṭivistārā pṛthivī kṛtsnataḥ smṛtā.
tasyā vārdhapramāṇena merorvai cāturantaram .. 50.68 ..
1.50.d:
शतार्द्ध कोटिविस्तारा पृथिवी कृत्स्नतः स्मृता।
तस्या वार्धप्रमाणेन मेरोर्वै चातुरन्तरम् ॥ 50.68 ॥
1.50.m: The earth in its entirety is considered to have an extent of fifty million [yojanas]. / By the measure of its half-ocean lies the distance from Meru to its four boundaries.

1.50.s:
pṛthivyā vārdhavistāro yojanāgrātprakīrttitaḥ .
merumadhyāt prati diśaṃ koṭirekādaśa smṛtāḥ .. 50.69 ..
1.50.d:
पृथिव्या वार्धविस्तारो योजनाग्रात्प्रकीर्त्तितः ।
मेरुमध्यात् प्रति दिशं कोटिरेकादश स्मृताः ॥ 50.69 ॥
1.50.m: Half the extent of the earth is proclaimed according to the total number of yojanas: / from the center of Meru toward each direction, it is considered eleven crores,

1.50.s:
tathā śatasahasrāṇi ekonanavatiḥ punaḥ.
pañcāśacca sahasrāṇi pṛthivyā vārdhavistaraḥ .. 50.70 ..
1.50.d:
तथा शतसहस्राणि एकोननवतिः पुनः।
पञ्चाशच्च सहस्राणि पृथिव्या वार्धविस्तरः ॥ 50.70 ॥
1.50.m: and eighty-nine hundred-thousands / and fifty thousand; [such] is half the extent of the earth.

1.50.s:
pṛthivyā vistaraṃ kṛtsnaṃ yojanaistannibodhata.
tisraḥ koṭyastu vistāraḥ saṃkhyātaḥ sa caturdiśam .. 50.71 ..
1.50.d:
पृथिव्या विस्तरं कृत्स्नं योजनैस्तन्निबोधत।
तिस्रः कोट्यस्तु विस्तारः संख्यातः स चतुर्दिशम् ॥ 50.71 ॥
1.50.m: Learn that full extent of the earth in yojanas: / the extent in the four directions is counted as three crores,

1.50.s:
tathā śatasahasrāṇāmekonāśītirucyate.
saptadvīpasamudrāyāḥ pṛthivyāstveṣa vistaraḥ .. 50.72 ..
1.50.d:
तथा शतसहस्राणामेकोनाशीतिरुच्यते।
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्रायाः पृथिव्यास्त्वेष विस्तरः ॥ 50.72 ॥
1.50.m: and seventy-nine hundred-thousands is said [to be added]. / This is the extent of the earth consisting of seven continents and oceans.

1.50.s:
vistārāt triguṇa़ñcaiva pṛthivyantasya maṇḍalam.
gaṇitaṃ yojanāgrantu koṭyastvekādaśa smṛtāḥ .. 50.73 ..
1.50.d:
विस्तारात् त्रिगुण़ञ्चैव पृथिव्यन्तस्य मण्डलम्।
गणितं योजनाग्रन्तु कोट्यस्त्वेकादश स्मृताः ॥ 50.73 ॥
1.50.m: And the circumference of the boundary of the earth is thrice the diameter; / the calculated sum of yojanas is considered eleven crores,

1.50.s:
tathā śatasahasrantu sapta triṃśādhikāni tu.
ityetadvai prasaṅkhyātaṃ pṛthivyantasya maṇḍalam .. 50.74 ..
1.50.d:
तथा शतसहस्रन्तु सप्त त्रिंशाधिकानि तु।
इत्येतद्वै प्रसङ्ख्यातं पृथिव्यन्तस्य मण्डलम् ॥ 50.74 ॥
1.50.m: and one hundred-thousand, plus thirty-seven [thousand]. / This is the calculated circumference of the boundary of the earth.

1.50.s:
tārakāsanniveśasya divi yāvaddhi maṇḍalam.
paryāsaḥ sanniveśasya bhūmastāvattu maṇḍalam .. 50.75 ..
1.50.d:
तारकासन्निवेशस्य दिवि यावद्धि मण्डलम्।
पर्यासः सन्निवेशस्य भूमस्तावत्तु मण्डलम् ॥ 50.75 ॥
1.50.m: As far as the circle of the arrangement of stars extends in the sky, / that far is the extent of the arrangement of the circle of the earth.

1.50.s:
paryāsapārimāṇḍena bhūmestulyaṃ divaṃ smṛtam.
saptānāmapi lokānāmetanmānaṃ prakīrtitam .. 50.76 ..
1.50.d:
पर्यासपारिमाण्डेन भूमेस्तुल्यं दिवं स्मृतम्।
सप्तानामपि लोकानामेतन्मानं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 50.76 ॥
1.50.m: Heaven is considered equal to the earth in the measure of its circumference. / This measurement is proclaimed for all seven worlds.

1.50.s:
paryāsapārimāṇḍena maṇḍalānugatena ca.
uparyupari lokānāṃ chatravatparimaṇḍalam .. 50.77 ..
1.50.d:
पर्यासपारिमाण्डेन मण्डलानुगतेन च।
उपर्युपरि लोकानां छत्रवत्परिमण्डलम् ॥ 50.77 ॥
1.50.m: By the measure of the circumference and corresponding to the circular form, / one above the other, the circular expanse of the worlds is like an umbrella,

1.50.s:
saṃsthitirvihitā sarvā yeṣu tiṣṭhanti jantavaḥ.
etadaṇḍakaṭāhasya pramāṇaṃ parikīrttitam .. 50.78 ..
1.50.d:
संस्थितिर्विहिता सर्वा येषु तिष्ठन्ति जन्तवः।
एतदण्डकटाहस्य प्रमाणं परिकीर्त्तितम् ॥ 50.78 ॥
1.50.m: the entire structure in which creatures dwell has been established. / This is proclaimed as the measure of the cosmic egg's shell.

1.50.s:
aṇḍasyāntastvime lokāḥ saptadvīpā ca medinī.
bhūrlokasva bhuvaścaiva tṛtīyaḥ svariti smṛtaḥ .
maharloko janaścaiva tapaḥ satyaśca saptamaḥ .. 50.79 ..
1.50.d:
अण्डस्यान्तस्त्विमे लोकाः सप्तद्वीपा च मेदिनी।
भूर्लोकस्व भुवश्चैव तृतीयः स्वरिति स्मृतः ।
महर्लोको जनश्चैव तपः सत्यश्च सप्तमः ॥ 50.79 ॥
1.50.m: Within the egg are these worlds, and the earth with seven continents: / the earth, the intermediate region, and heaven is known as the third, / Maharloka, Janas, Tapas, and Satya is the seventh.

1.50.s:
ete sapta kṛtā lokāśchatrākārā vyavasthitāḥ.
svakairāvaraṇaiḥ sūkṣmairdhāryamāṇāḥ pṛthak pṛthak .. 50.80 ..
1.50.d:
एते सप्त कृता लोकाश्छत्राकारा व्यवस्थिताः।
स्वकैरावरणैः सूक्ष्मैर्धार्यमाणाः पृथक् पृथक् ॥ 50.80 ॥
1.50.m: These seven worlds have been made situated in the shape of umbrellas, / held up separately by their own subtle coverings,

1.50.s:
daśabhāgādhikābhiśca tābhiḥ prakṛtibhirbahiḥ.
dhāryamāṇā viśeṣaiśca samutpannaiḥ parasparam .. 50.81 ..
1.50.d:
दशभागाधिकाभिश्च ताभिः प्रकृतिभिर्बहिः।
धार्यमाणा विशेषैश्च समुत्पन्नैः परस्परम् ॥ 50.81 ॥
1.50.m: and held outside by those primal elements, each ten times greater than the last, / and by specific principles evolved from one another.

1.50.s:
asyāṇḍasya samantācca sanniviṣṭo ghanodadhiḥ.
pṛthivīmaṇḍalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ ghanatoyena dhāryate .. 50.82 ..
1.50.d:
अस्याण्डस्य समन्ताच्च सन्निविष्टो घनोदधिः।
पृथिवीमण्डलं कृत्स्नं घनतोयेन धार्यते ॥ 50.82 ॥
1.50.m: All around this cosmic egg is situated the dense ocean; / the entire circle of the earth is supported by dense water.

1.50.s:
ghanodadhipareṇātha dhāryyate ghanatejasā.
bāhyato ghanatejastu tiryyagūrddhvantu maṇḍalam .. 50.83 ..
1.50.d:
घनोदधिपरेणाथ धार्य्यते घनतेजसा।
बाह्यतो घनतेजस्तु तिर्य्यगूर्द्ध्वन्तु मण्डलम् ॥ 50.83 ॥
1.50.m: Beyond the dense ocean, it is supported by dense fire; / and outside, the sphere of dense fire extends diagonally and upward.

1.50.s:
samantādvanavātena dhāryyamāṇaṃ pratiṣṭhitam.
ghanavātāttathākāśamākāśañca mahātmanā .. 50.84 ..
1.50.d:
समन्ताद्वनवातेन धार्य्यमाणं प्रतिष्ठितम्।
घनवातात्तथाकाशमाकाशञ्च महात्मना ॥ 50.84 ॥
1.50.m: Supported on all sides by dense air, it is firmly established; / after the dense wind is the ether, and the ether [is encompassed] by the Great Self;

1.50.s:
bhūtādinā vṛtaṃ sarvvaṃ bhūtādhirmahatā vṛtaḥ .
vṛto mahānanantena pradhānenāvyayātmanā .. 50.85 ..
1.50.d:
भूतादिना वृतं सर्व्वं भूताधिर्महता वृतः ।
वृतो महाननन्तेन प्रधानेनाव्ययात्मना ॥ 50.85 ॥
1.50.m: everything is enveloped by the origin of elements (ego), and the origin of elements is enveloped by the cosmic intellect (mahat); / the great intellect is enveloped by the endless, unmanifest primal matter (pradhāna), imperishable by nature.

1.50.s:
purāṇi lokapālānāṃ pravakṣyāmi yathākramam .
jyotirgaṇapracārasya pramāṇaṃ parivakṣyate .. 50.86 ..
1.50.d:
पुराणि लोकपालानां प्रवक्ष्यामि यथाक्रमम् ।
ज्योतिर्गणप्रचारस्य प्रमाणं परिवक्ष्यते ॥ 50.86 ॥
1.50.m: I shall describe the cities of the world-guardians in proper order; / the extent of the movement of the hosts of luminaries will be proclaimed.

1.50.s:
meroḥ prācyāṃ diśi tathā mānasasyaiva mūrddhani.
vasvokasārā māhendrī puṇyā hemapariṣkṛtā . 50.87 ..
1.50.d:
मेरोः प्राच्यां दिशि तथा मानसस्यैव मूर्द्धनि।
वस्वोकसारा माहेन्द्री पुण्या हेमपरिष्कृता । 50.87 ॥
1.50.m: To the east of Meru, upon the summit of Mānasa, / is Vasvokasārā, the sacred city of Indra, adorned with gold.

1.50.s:
dakṣiṇena punarmerormānasasyaiva mūrddhani.
vaivasvato nivasati yamaḥ saṃyamane pure .. 50.88 ..
1.50.d:
दक्षिणेन पुनर्मेरोर्मानसस्यैव मूर्द्धनि।
वैवस्वतो निवसति यमः संयमने पुरे ॥ 50.88 ॥
1.50.m:
South of Meru, however, upon the summit of Mānasa,
dwells Yama, son of Vivasvat, in the city Saṃyamana.

1.50.s:
pratīcyāntu punarmerormānasasyaiva mūrddhani.
sukhā nāma purī ramyā varuṇasyātha dhīmataḥ .. 50.89 ..
1.50.d:
प्रतीच्यान्तु पुनर्मेरोर्मानसस्यैव मूर्द्धनि।
सुखा नाम पुरी रम्या वरुणस्याथ धीमतः ॥ 50.89 ॥
1.50.m:
West of Meru, on the summit of Mānasa,
stands the delightful city named Sukhā, belonging to wise Varuṇa.

1.50.s:
diśyuttarasyāṃ merostu mānasasyaiva mūrddhani.
tulyā māhendrapuryyā tu somasyāpi vibhāvarī .. 50.90 ..
1.50.d:
दिश्युत्तरस्यां मेरोस्तु मानसस्यैव मूर्द्धनि।
तुल्या माहेन्द्रपुर्य्या तु सोमस्यापि विभावरी ॥ 50.90 ॥
1.50.m:
In the northern quarter from Meru, on the summit of Mānasa,
is Soma's city Vibhāvarī, equal to the city of Mahendra.

1.50.s:
mānasottarapṛṣṭhe tu lokapālāścaturddiśam.
sthitā dharmmavyavasthāyai lokasaṃrakṣaṇāya ca .. 50.91 ..
1.50.d:
मानसोत्तरपृष्ठे तु लोकपालाश्चतुर्द्दिशम्।
स्थिता धर्म्मव्यवस्थायै लोकसंरक्षणाय च ॥ 50.91 ॥
1.50.m:
Upon the Mānasa mountain, the guardians of the world stand in the four quarters
for the maintenance of dharma and the protection of the worlds.

1.50.s:
lokapālopariṣṭāttu sarvvato dakṣiṇāyane.
kāṣṭhāgatasya sūryyasya gatiryā tāṃ nibodhata .. 50.92 ..
1.50.d:
लोकपालोपरिष्टात्तु सर्व्वतो दक्षिणायने।
काष्ठागतस्य सूर्य्यस्य गतिर्या तां निबोधत ॥ 50.92 ॥
1.50.m:
Above the guardians of the world everywhere during the southern course,
understand the movement of the sun when it has reached its farthest point.

1.50.s:
dakṣiṇe prakrame sūryyaḥ kṣipteṣuriva sarpati.
jyotiṣāñcakramādāya satataṃ parigacchati .. 50.93 ..
1.50.d:
दक्षिणे प्रक्रमे सूर्य्यः क्षिप्तेषुरिव सर्पति।
ज्योतिषाञ्चक्रमादाय सततं परिगच्छति ॥ 50.93 ॥
1.50.m:
In its southern course, the sun glides like a released arrow;
taking along the circle of celestial bodies, it moves constantly around.

1.50.s:
madhyagaścāmarāvatyāṃ yadā bhavati bhāskaraḥ.
vaivasvate saṃyamane udayastatra ucyate .. 50.94 ..
1.50.d:
मध्यगश्चामरावत्यां यदा भवति भास्करः।
वैवस्वते संयमने उदयस्तत्र उच्यते ॥ 50.94 ॥
1.50.m:
When the sun is at the zenith in Amarāvatī,
that is declared to be dawn in Saṃyamana, belonging to the son of Vivasvat.

1.50.s:
sukhāyāmarddharātrañca madhyagaḥ syādraviryadā.
sukhāyāmatha vāruṇyāmuttiṣṭhan sa tu dṛśyate .. 50.95 ..
1.50.d:
सुखायामर्द्धरात्रञ्च मध्यगः स्याद्रविर्यदा।
सुखायामथ वारुण्यामुत्तिष्ठन् स तु दृश्यते ॥ 50.95 ॥
1.50.m:
And when it is midnight in Sukhā, the sun is at the zenith [in Amarāvatī];
then in Sukhā, belonging to Varuṇa, he is seen rising.

1.50.s:
vibhāyāmarddharātraṃ syānmāhendyrāmastameti ca.
tadā dakṣiṇapūrvveṣāmaparāhno vidhīyate .. 50.96 ..
1.50.d:
विभायामर्द्धरात्रं स्यान्माहेन्द्य्रामस्तमेति च।
तदा दक्षिणपूर्व्वेषामपराह्नो विधीयते ॥ 50.96 ॥
1.50.m:
When it is midnight in Vibhā, it sets in Māhendrī;
then for those in the south-east the afternoon is ordained.

1.50.s:
dakṣiṇāpara deśyānāṃ pūrvvāhnaḥ parikīrttyate.
teṣāmapararātrañca ye janā uttarāpathe .. 50.97 ..
1.50.d:
दक्षिणापर देश्यानां पूर्व्वाह्नः परिकीर्त्त्यते।
तेषामपररात्रञ्च ये जना उत्तरापथे ॥ 50.97 ॥
1.50.m:
For the people of the south-western regions the forenoon is proclaimed;
and for those people who dwell on the northern path it is the latter part of the night.

1.50.s:
deśā uttarapūrvvā ye pūrvvarātrantu tān prati.
evamevottareṣvarko bhavaneṣu virājate .. 50.98 ..
1.50.d:
देशा उत्तरपूर्व्वा ये पूर्व्वरात्रन्तु तान् प्रति।
एवमेवोत्तरेष्वर्को भवनेषु विराजते ॥ 50.98 ॥
1.50.m:
For those regions which are in the north-east it is the first part of the night.
In this very manner the sun shines over the northern dwellings.

1.50.s:
sukhāyāmatha vāruṇyāṃ madhyāhne cāryyamā yadā.
vibhāvaryyāṃ somapuryyāmuttiṣṭhati vibhāvasuḥ .. 50.99 ..
1.50.d:
सुखायामथ वारुण्यां मध्याह्ने चार्य्यमा यदा।
विभावर्य्यां सोमपुर्य्यामुत्तिष्ठति विभावसुः ॥ 50.99 ॥
1.50.m:
When Aryaman is at midday in Sukhā, belonging to Varuṇa,
the sun rises in Vibhāvarī, the city of Soma.

1.50.s:
rātryarddhaṃ cāmarāvatyāmastameti yamasya ca.
somapuryāṃ vibhāyāntu madhyāhne syāddhivākaraḥ .. 50.100 ..
1.50.d:
रात्र्यर्द्धं चामरावत्यामस्तमेति यमस्य च।
सोमपुर्यां विभायान्तु मध्याह्ने स्याद्धिवाकरः ॥ 50.100 ॥
1.50.m:
It is midnight in Amarāvatī, and it sets for Yama;
and in the city of Soma, Vibhā, the sun is at midday.

1.50.s:
mahendrasyāmarāvatyāmuttiṣṭhati yadā raviḥ.
arddharātraṃ saṃyamane vāruṇyāmastameti ca .. 50.101 ..
1.50.d:
महेन्द्रस्यामरावत्यामुत्तिष्ठति यदा रविः।
अर्द्धरात्रं संयमने वारुण्यामस्तमेति च ॥ 50.101 ॥
1.50.m:
When the sun rises in Amarāvatī of Mahendra,
it is midnight in Saṃyamana, and it sets in [the city] belonging to Varuṇa.

1.50.s:
sa śīgrameti paryyeti bhāskaro'lātacakravat.
bhraman vai bhramamāṇāni ṛkṣāṇi gagane raviḥ .. 50.102 ..
1.50.d:
स शीग्रमेति पर्य्येति भास्करोऽलातचक्रवत्।
भ्रमन् वै भ्रममाणानि ऋक्षाणि गगने रविः ॥ 50.102 ॥
1.50.m:
The sun moves swiftly around like a whirling firebrand,
the revolving sun wheeling with the revolving constellations in the sky.

1.50.s:
evaṃ caturṣu dvīpeṣu dakṣiṇāntena sarpati.
udayāstamanenāsāvuttiṣṭhati punaḥ punaḥ .. 50.103 ..
1.50.d:
एवं चतुर्षु द्वीपेषु दक्षिणान्तेन सर्पति।
उदयास्तमनेनासावुत्तिष्ठति पुनः पुनः ॥ 50.103 ॥
1.50.m:
Thus across the four continents it glides along the southern limit;
by rising and setting, it rises again and again.

1.50.s:
pūrvvāhne cāparāhne tu dvau dvau devālayau tu saḥ.
tapatyekantu madhyāhne taireva tu saraśmibhiḥ .. 50.104 ..
1.50.d:
पूर्व्वाह्ने चापराह्ने तु द्वौ द्वौ देवालयौ तु सः।
तपत्येकन्तु मध्याह्ने तैरेव तु सरश्मिभिः ॥ 50.104 ॥
1.50.m:
In the forenoon and afternoon it shines upon two abodes of the gods [at a time],
but at midday it shines upon only one with those very rays.

1.50.s:
udito varddhamānābhirāmadhyāhnaṃ tapan raviḥ.
ataḥ paraṃ hrasantībhirgobhirastaṃ sa gacchati .. 50.105 ..
1.50.d:
उदितो वर्द्धमानाभिरामध्याह्नं तपन् रविः।
अतः परं ह्रसन्तीभिर्गोभिरस्तं स गच्छति ॥ 50.105 ॥
1.50.m:
Having risen, scorching until midday with increasing rays,
thereafter with diminishing rays the sun goes to its setting.

1.50.s:
udayāstamayābhyāṃ hismṛte pūrvāpare diśo.
yāvatpurastāttapati tāvat pṛṣṭhe tu pārśvayoḥ .. 50.106 ..
1.50.d:
उदयास्तमयाभ्यां हिस्मृते पूर्वापरे दिशो।
यावत्पुरस्तात्तपति तावत् पृष्ठे तु पार्श्वयोः ॥ 50.106 ॥
1.50.m:
By rising and setting indeed the east and west directions are defined;
as far as it shines in front, so far does it shine behind and on both flanks.

1.50.s:
yatrodyan dṛśyate sūryasteṣāṃ sa udayaḥ smṛtaḥ.
yatra praṇāśamāyāti teṣāmastaḥ sa ucyate .. 50.107 ..
1.50.d:
यत्रोद्यन् दृश्यते सूर्यस्तेषां स उदयः स्मृतः।
यत्र प्रणाशमायाति तेषामस्तः स उच्यते ॥ 50.107 ॥
1.50.m:
Where the sun is seen rising, for them that is remembered as sunrise;
where it disappears, for them that is called sunset.

1.50.s:
sarveṣāmuttare merurlokālokastu dakṣiṇe.
vidūrabhāvādarkasya bhūmerlekhāvṛtasya ca.
hriyante raśmayo yasmāttena rātrau na dṛśyate .. 50.108 ..
1.50.d:
सर्वेषामुत्तरे मेरुर्लोकालोकस्तु दक्षिणे।
विदूरभावादर्कस्य भूमेर्लेखावृतस्य च।
ह्रियन्ते रश्मयो यस्मात्तेन रात्रौ न दृश्यते ॥ 50.108 ॥
1.50.m:
Meru is to the north of all, and Lokāloka to the south.
Because of the distance from the sun and because the earth is bounded by a line,
its rays are obstructed, wherefore it is not seen at night.

1.50.s:
grahanakṣatratārāṇāṃ darśanaṃ bhāskarasya ca.
ucchrāyasya pramāṇena jñeyamastamanodayam .. 50.109 ..
1.50.d:
ग्रहनक्षत्रताराणां दर्शनं भास्करस्य च।
उच्छ्रायस्य प्रमाणेन ज्ञेयमस्तमनोदयम् ॥ 50.109 ॥
1.50.m:
The sight of the planets, constellations, and stars, and of the sun,
their setting and rising, is to be known by the measure of altitude.

1.50.s:
śuklacchāyognirāpaśca kṛṣṇacchāyā ca medinī.
vidūrabhāvādarkasya udyātasya viraśmitā.
raktābāvo viraśmitvādraktatvāccāpyanuṣṇatā .. 50.110 ..
1.50.d:
शुक्लच्छायोग्निरापश्च कृष्णच्छाया च मेदिनी।
विदूरभावादर्कस्य उद्यातस्य विरश्मिता।
रक्ताबावो विरश्मित्वाद्रक्तत्वाच्चाप्यनुष्णता ॥ 50.110 ॥

1.50.s:
lekhayāvasthitaḥ sūryo yatra yatra tu dṛśyate.
ūrddhvaṃ gataḥ sahasrantu yojanānāṃ sa dṛśyate .. 50.111 ..
1.50.d:
लेखयावस्थितः सूर्यो यत्र यत्र तु दृश्यते।
ऊर्द्ध्वं गतः सहस्रन्तु योजनानां स दृश्यते ॥ 50.111 ॥
1.50.m:
Wherever the sun, stationed on the horizon, is seen,
having ascended a thousand yojanas it is [still] seen.

1.50.s:
prabhā hi saurī pādena astaṅgacchati bhāskare.
agnimāviśate rātrau tasmāddūrāt prakāśate .. 50.112 ..
1.50.d:
प्रभा हि सौरी पादेन अस्तङ्गच्छति भास्करे।
अग्निमाविशते रात्रौ तस्माद्दूरात् प्रकाशते ॥ 50.112 ॥
1.50.m:
For when the sun goes to its setting, its brilliance with a quarter [part]
enters fire at night; therefore fire shines from afar.

1.50.s:
uditastu punaḥ sūryaḥ astamāgneyamāviśat.
saṃyukto vahninā sūryastataḥ sa tapate divā .. 50.113 ..
1.50.d:
उदितस्तु पुनः सूर्यः अस्तमाग्नेयमाविशत्।
संयुक्तो वह्निना सूर्यस्ततः स तपते दिवा ॥ 50.113 ॥
1.50.m:
When the sun has risen again, it enters the setting fire;
united with fire, the sun then scorches by day.

1.50.s:
prākāśyañca tathauṣṇyañca sūryāgneyī ca tejasī.
parasparānupraveśādāpyāyete divāniśam .. 50.114 ..
1.50.d:
प्राकाश्यञ्च तथौष्ण्यञ्च सूर्याग्नेयी च तेजसी।
परस्परानुप्रवेशादाप्यायेते दिवानिशम् ॥ 50.114 ॥
1.50.m:
Luminosity and heat, the solar and fiery energies,
increase each other night and day by mutually penetrating each other.

1.50.s:
uttare caiva bhūmyarddhe tathā tasmiṃśca dakṣiṇe.
uttiṣṭhati tathā sūrye rātrirāviśate tvapaḥ .
tasmāttāmrā bhavantyāpo divārātripraveśanāt .. 50.115 ..
1.50.d:
उत्तरे चैव भूम्यर्द्धे तथा तस्मिंश्च दक्षिणे।
उत्तिष्ठति तथा सूर्ये रात्रिराविशते त्वपः ।
तस्मात्ताम्रा भवन्त्यापो दिवारात्रिप्रवेशनात् ॥ 50.115 ॥

1.50.s:
astaṃ yāti punaḥ sūrye dinaṃ vai praviśatyapaḥ.
tasmācchuklā bhavantyāpo naktamahnaḥ praveśanāt .. 50.116 ..
1.50.d:
अस्तं याति पुनः सूर्ये दिनं वै प्रविशत्यपः।
तस्माच्छुक्ला भवन्त्यापो नक्तमह्नः प्रवेशनात् ॥ 50.116 ॥
1.50.m:
When the sun goes to its setting, day enters the waters;
therefore the waters become white at night from the entrance of day.

1.50.s:
etena kramayogena bhūmyarddhe dakṣiṇottare.
udayāstamane'rkasya ahorātraṃ viśatyapaḥ .. 50.117 ..
1.50.d:
एतेन क्रमयोगेन भूम्यर्द्धे दक्षिणोत्तरे।
उदयास्तमनेऽर्कस्य अहोरात्रं विशत्यपः ॥ 50.117 ॥
1.50.m:
By this regular sequence in the southern and northern halves of the earth,
day and night enter the waters at the rising and setting of the sun.

1.50.s:
dinaṃ sūryaprakāśākhyaṃ tāmasī rātrirucyate.
tasmādvyavasthitā rātriḥ sūryāvekṣyamahaḥ smṛtam .. 50.118.
evaṃ puṣkaramadhyena yadā sarpati bhāskaraḥ.
triṃśāṃ śakantu medinyā muhūrtenaiva gacchati .. 50.119 ..
1.50.d:
दिनं सूर्यप्रकाशाख्यं तामसी रात्रिरुच्यते।
तस्माद्व्यवस्थिता रात्रिः सूर्यावेक्ष्यमहः स्मृतम् ॥ 50.118.
एवं पुष्करमध्येन यदा सर्पति भास्करः।
त्रिंशां शकन्तु मेदिन्या मुहूर्तेनैव गच्छति ॥ 50.119 ॥
1.50.m:
Day is designated as the light of the sun; night is said to be dark.
Therefore night is fixed, and day is remembered as depending on the sun.

In this way, when the sun moves through the middle of Puṣkara,
it traverses a thirtieth part of the earth in a single muhūrta.

1.50.s:
yojanāgrānmuhūrttasya imāṃ saṅkhyāṃ nibodhata.
pūrṇaṃ śatasahasrāṇāmekatriṃśattu sā smṛtā .. 50.120 ..
1.50.d:
योजनाग्रान्मुहूर्त्तस्य इमां सङ्ख्यां निबोधत।
पूर्णं शतसहस्राणामेकत्रिंशत्तु सा स्मृता ॥ 50.120 ॥
1.50.m:
Learn this calculation of the total yojanas of a muhūrta:
it is remembered as thirty-one full hundreds of thousands,

1.50.s:
pañcāśattu tathānyāni sahasrāṇyadhikāni tu.
mauhūrttikī gatirhyeṣā sūryasya tu vidhīyate .. 50.121 ..
1.50.d:
पञ्चाशत्तु तथान्यानि सहस्राण्यधिकानि तु।
मौहूर्त्तिकी गतिर्ह्येषा सूर्यस्य तु विधीयते ॥ 50.121 ॥
1.50.m:
and fifty other thousands in addition;
for this is prescribed as the movement of the sun in a single muhūrta.

1.50.s:
etena gatiyogena yadā kāṣṭhāntu dakṣiṇām.
paryyāgacchettadādityo māghe kāṣṭhāntameva hi .. 50.122 ..
1.50.d:
एतेन गतियोगेन यदा काष्ठान्तु दक्षिणाम्।
पर्य्यागच्छेत्तदादित्यो माघे काष्ठान्तमेव हि ॥ 50.122 ॥
1.50.m:
When, by this rate of motion, the sun traverses the southern limit,
then, in Māgha, the sun reaches the very end of the limit.

1.50.s:
sarpate dakṣiṇāyāntu kāṣṭhāyāṃ tannibodhata.
navakoṭyaḥ prasaṅkhyātā yojanaiḥ parimaṇḍalam .. 50.123 ..
1.50.d:
सर्पते दक्षिणायान्तु काष्ठायां तन्निबोधत।
नवकोट्यः प्रसङ्ख्याता योजनैः परिमण्डलम् ॥ 50.123 ॥
1.50.m:
Understand that when it glides along the southern limit,
its circumference is calculated at nine crores of yojanas,

1.50.s:
tathā śatasahasrāṇi catvāriṃśacca pañca ca.
ahorātrātpataṅgasya gatireṣā vidhīyate .. 50.124 ..
1.50.d:
तथा शतसहस्राणि चत्वारिंशच्च पञ्च च।
अहोरात्रात्पतङ्गस्य गतिरेषा विधीयते ॥ 50.124 ॥
1.50.m:
and likewise forty-five hundred-thousands;
this is ordained as the movement of the sun in a day and a night.

1.50.s:
dakṣiṇādvinivṛtto'sau viṣuvastho yadā raviḥ.
kṣīrodasya samudrasya uttarāntā diśaścaran .. 50.125 ..
1.50.d:
दक्षिणाद्विनिवृत्तोऽसौ विषुवस्थो यदा रविः।
क्षीरोदस्य समुद्रस्य उत्तरान्ता दिशश्चरन् ॥ 50.125 ॥
1.50.m:
When the sun, having turned back from the south, is stationed on the equinox,
moving along the northern edge of the Milk Ocean,

1.50.s:
maṇḍalaṃ viṣuvadyāpi yojanaistannibodhata.
tisraḥ koṭyastu vistīrṇā viṣuvadyāpi sā smṛtā .. 50.126 ..
1.50.d:
मण्डलं विषुवद्यापि योजनैस्तन्निबोधत।
तिस्रः कोट्यस्तु विस्तीर्णा विषुवद्यापि सा स्मृता ॥ 50.126 ॥
1.50.m:
understand that circle which spans the equinox in yojanas:
that which spans the equinox is remembered as extended to three crores,

1.50.s:
tathā śatasahasrāṇāmaśītyekādhikā punaḥ .
śravaṇe cottarāṃ kāṣṭhāñcitrabhānuryadā bhavet .
śākadvīpasya ṣaṣṭhasya uttarāntā diśaścaran .. 50.127 ..
1.50.d:
तथा शतसहस्राणामशीत्येकाधिका पुनः ।
श्रवणे चोत्तरां काष्ठाञ्चित्रभानुर्यदा भवेत् ।
शाकद्वीपस्य षष्ठस्य उत्तरान्ता दिशश्चरन् ॥ 50.127 ॥
1.50.m:
and in addition eighty-one hundred-thousands.
And when Citrabhānu [the sun] reaches the northern limit in Śravaṇa,
moving along the northern edge of the sixth [continent], Śākadvīpa,

1.50.s:
uttarāyāñca kāṣṭhāyāṃ pramāṇaṃ maṇ‍ḍalasya ca.
yojanāgrātprasaṅkhyātā koṭirekā tu sā dvijaiḥ .. 50.128 ..
1.50.d:
उत्तरायाञ्च काष्ठायां प्रमाणं मण्‍डलस्य च।
योजनाग्रात्प्रसङ्ख्याता कोटिरेका तु सा द्विजैः ॥ 50.128 ॥
1.50.m:
the measure of the circle at the northern limit
is calculated in total yojanas by the twice-born as one crore,

1.50.s:
aśītirniyutānīha yojanānāṃ tathaiva ca.
aṣṭapañcāśatañcaiva yojanānyadhikāni tu .. 50.129 ..
1.50.d:
अशीतिर्नियुतानीह योजनानां तथैव च।
अष्टपञ्चाशतञ्चैव योजनान्यधिकानि तु ॥ 50.129 ॥
1.50.m:
and likewise eighty niyutas of yojanas here,
and fifty-eight yojanas in addition.

1.50.s:
nāgavīthyuttarāvīthī ajavīthī ca dakṣiṇā.
mūlaṃ caiva tathāṣāḍe hyajavīthyudayāstrayaḥ.
abhijitpūrvataḥ svātirnāgavīthyudayāstrayaḥ .. 50.130 ..
1.50.d:
नागवीथ्युत्तरावीथी अजवीथी च दक्षिणा।
मूलं चैव तथाषाडे ह्यजवीथ्युदयास्त्रयः।
अभिजित्पूर्वतः स्वातिर्नागवीथ्युदयास्त्रयः ॥ 50.130 ॥

1.50.s:
kāṣṭhayorantaraṃ yacca tadvakṣye yojanaiḥ punaḥ.
etacchatasahasrāṇāmekatriṃśottaraṃ śatam .. 50.131 ..
1.50.d:
काष्ठयोरन्तरं यच्च तद्वक्ष्ये योजनैः पुनः।
एतच्छतसहस्राणामेकत्रिंशोत्तरं शतम् ॥ 50.131 ॥
1.50.m:
And the distance between the two cardinal limits I shall tell again in yojanas:
this is one hundred and thirty-one hundred-thousands [13,100,000],

1.50.s:
